title: Keritot 7
description: Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis on a priest’s daughter who loses her status, anointing oil moved on the High Priest’s own body, whether Yom Kippur atones for one who rejects it or does not repent, the blasphemer’s offering, and a new mishna on which miscarriages oblige a woman’s offering.
topics: 👑 A priest’s daughter married to an Israelite or to one unfit for her: the fifth, and burning or strangulation
🫒 Oil from the High Priest’s head placed on his stomach, and teruma oil a grandson may rub against
🕯️ Does Yom Kippur atone for one who rejects it, or who does not repent?
🔁 “My sin offering should not atone for me”: Abaye, Rava, and Rava’s retraction
⏳ Rabbi’s view, and how karet for Yom Kippur itself can still be found
🗣️ The blasphemer: Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis, Isi ben Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
🕊️ Miscarriages: an offering that is eaten, one that is not, or none; Rabbi Yosei’s stipulation
🌙 A miscarriage on the night of the eighty-first day: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel

a1.he: בַּת כֹּהֵן שֶׁנִּישֵּׂאת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאָכְלָה בִּתְרוּמָה – מְשַׁלֶּמֶת אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְאֵינָהּ מְשַׁלֶּמֶת אֶת הַחוֹמֶשׁ, וּמִיתָתָהּ בִּשְׂרֵיפָה.

a2.he: נִיסֵּת לְאֶחָד מִן הַפְּסוּלִין – מְשַׁלֶּמֶת קֶרֶן וָחוֹמֶשׁ, וּמִיתָתָהּ בְּחֶנֶק, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.

a3.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ מְשַׁלֶּמֶת [אֶת] הַקֶּרֶן וְאֵינָהּ מְשַׁלֶּמֶת [אֶת] הַחוֹמֶשׁ, וּמִיתָתָהּ בִּשְׂרֵיפָה.

a4.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַחְלוֹקֶת בִּנְתִינַת שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה וּבְשִׁינּוּיֵי דְּשַׁנִּינַן, אֲבָל נְתִינָה דְּעָלְמָא – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל כְּזַיִת.

a5.he: גּוּפָא. תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּסָךְ – יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּבַל יִיסָךְ, וְכׇל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּסָךְ – אֵינוֹ בְּבַל יִיסָךְ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ, ״לֹא יִיסָךְ״ כְּתִיב, וּקְרִי בֵּיהּ ״לֹא יַסִּיךְ״.

a6.he: תָּנֵי רַב חֲנַנְיָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא: מִנַּיִן לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁנָּטַל מִשֶּׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה שֶׁעַל רֹאשׁוֹ וְנָתַן עַל בְּנֵי מֵעָיו, מִנַּיִן שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עַל בְּשַׂר אָדָם לֹא יִיסָךְ״. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי שְׁנָא מֵהָא דְּתַנְיָא: כֹּהֵן שֶׁסָּךְ בְּשֶׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, בֶּן בִּתּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִתְעַגֵּל בּוֹ וְאֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ?

a7.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם, ״וּמֵתוּ בוֹ כִּי יְחַלְּלֻהוּ״ כְּתִיב – כֵּיוָן דְּחַלְּלֵיהּ הָא אִיתַּחַיל, אֲבָל גַּבֵּי שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה כְּתִיב: ״כִּי נֵזֶר [שֶׁמֶן מִשְׁחַת] אֱלֹהָיו עָלָיו״ – ״שֶׁמֶן מִשְׁחָה״ קַרְיֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא, דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיתֵיהּ עָלָיו לָא אִיתַּחַיל.

a8.he: עַל אֵלּוּ חַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹנוֹ כּוּ׳. קָתָנֵי: חוּץ מִמְּטַמֵּא מִקְדָּשׁ וְקָדָשָׁיו. מִמַּאי מַפֵּיק לֵיהּ? הָכִי קָתָנֵי: חוּץ מִמִּטַּמֵּא מִקְדָּשׁ וְקָדָשָׁיו, שֶׁאֵין מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי.

a9.he: וְנִיתְנֵי נָמֵי: חוּץ מִמִּי שֶׁעָבַר עָלָיו יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים, שֶׁאֵין מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי! אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כִּי קָתָנֵי, הֵיכָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ לַחֲטָאֵהּ וְרַחֲמָנָא פַּטְרֵיהּ. עָבַר עָלָיו יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים לֵיתֵיהּ לַחֲטָאֵהּ, דְּקָא כַפַּר לֵיהּ.

a10.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בִּמְבַעֵט, דְּקָאָמַר: אֵין יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר, דְּאִי הָדַר בֵּיהּ בָּתַר יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים, בָּעֵי לְאֵיתוֹיֵי אָשָׁם תָּלוּי. וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ סָבַר: מְבַעֵט נָמֵי מְכַפַּר עֲלֵיהּ יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים.

a11.he: וּבִפְלוּגְתָּא: הָאוֹמֵר: ״לֹא יִתְכַּפֵּר לִי חַטָּאתִי״, אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֵינָהּ מְכַפֶּרֶת, רָבָא אָמַר: מְכַפֶּרֶת. הֵיכָא דְּאָמַר: ״לֹא תִּיקְרַב״ – דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלָא מְכַפְּרָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״יַקְרִיב אוֹתוֹ״ – לִרְצוֹנוֹ. כִּי פְּלִיגִי, דְּאָמַר: ״תִּיקְרַב וְלֹא תְּכַפֵּר״, אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֵין מְכַפֶּרֶת, דְּהָא אָמַר לֹא תְּכַפֵּר. רָבָא אָמַר: מְכַפֶּרֶת, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר תִּיקְרַב – כַּפָּרָה מִמֵּילָא (אָתֵי).

a12.he: וַהֲדַר בֵּיהּ רָבָא, כִּדְתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יְהֵא יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר עַל שָׁבִין וְעַל שֶׁאֵין שָׁבִין? וְדִין הוּא, וּמָה חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם מְכַפְּרִין וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר, מָה חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם אֵין מְכַפְּרִין אֶלָּא עַל הַשָּׁבִין אַף יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אֵין מְכַפֵּר אֶלָּא עַל הַשָּׁבִין!

a13.he: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם, שֶׁאֵין מְכַפְּרִין עַל הַמֵּזִיד כַּשּׁוֹגֵג, תֹּאמַר בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, שֶׁמְּכַפֵּר עַל הַמֵּזִיד כַּשּׁוֹגֵג. וְהוֹאִיל וּמְכַפֵּר עַל הַמֵּזִיד כַּשּׁוֹגֵג, מְכַפֵּר עַל שָׁבִין וְעַל שֶׁאֵין שָׁבִין! תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אַךְ״, חָלַק.

a14.he: מַאי ״שָׁבִין״ וְ״שֶׁאֵין שָׁבִין״? אִלֵּימָא ״שָׁבִין״ – שׁוֹגֵג, ״לֹא שָׁבִין״ – מֵזִיד, הָא קָתָנֵי: לֹא אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם כּוּ׳!

a15.he: אֶלָּא, כִּי הָא דְּעוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָכַל חֵלֶב וְהִפְרִישׁ קׇרְבָּן, וְנִשְׁתַּמֵּד וְחָזַר בּוֹ, הוֹאִיל וְנִדְחָה – יִדָּחֶה.

a16.he: נְהִי דְּאִידְּחִי קׇרְבָּן, גַּבְרָא בַּר כַּפָּרָה הוּא! אֶלָּא ״שָׁבִין״ – דְּאָמַר: ״יְכַפֵּר עָלַי חַטָּאתִי״, ״שֶׁאֵין שָׁבִין״ – דְּאָמַר: ״לֹא תְּכַפֵּר עָלַי חַטָּאתִי״, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ:

a17.he: וּרְמִינְהִי: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר אֶלָּא עַל שֶׁנִּתְעַנָּה בּוֹ וְלֹא עָשָׂה בּוֹ מְלָאכָה וּקְרָאוֹ מִקְרָא קוֹדֶשׁ, לֹא נִתְעַנָּה בּוֹ וְעָשָׂה בּוֹ מְלָאכָה וְלֹא קְרָאוֹ מִקְרָא קוֹדֶשׁ יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא יוֹם כִּיפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא״, מִכׇּל מָקוֹם. וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ סְתָם סִיפְרָא הוּא, קַשְׁיָין אַהֲדָדֵי!

a18.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא – רַבִּי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא – רַבִּי אַלִּיבָּא דִּידֵיהּ, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה, בֵּין עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה וּבֵין לֹא עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה – יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר,

a19.he: חוּץ מִפּוֹרֵק עוֹל, וּמְגַלֶּה פָּנִים בַּתּוֹרָה, וּמֵפֵר בְּרִית בָּשָׂר, שֶׁאִם עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה – יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר, וְאִם לָאו – אֵין יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר.

a20.he: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי אַלִּיבָּא דְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ, וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי בַּעֲבֵירוֹת דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים גּוּפֵיהּ – דְּלָא מְכַפַּר. דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, כָּרֵת דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לְרַבִּי, כֵּיוָן דִּבְכֹל שַׁעְתָּא וְשַׁעְתָּא מְכַפַּר, הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ?

a21.he: וּמַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּילְמָא דַּעֲבַד עֲבִידְתָּא כּוּלֵּי לֵילְיָא וּבַהֲדֵי עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר מִית, דְּלָא הֲוָה יְמָמָא דִּלְכַפַּר לֵיהּ! תִּינַח כָּרֵת דְּלֵילְיָא, כָּרֵת דִּימָמָא הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ?

a22.he: וּמַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּילְמָא בַּהֲדֵי דְּקָאָכַל נַהֲמָא חֲנַקְתֵּיהּ אוּמְצָא, דְּלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ שְׁהוּת בִּימָמָא דִּלְכַפַּר לֵיהּ. אִי נָמֵי, דַּעֲבַד עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ סָמוּךְ לִשְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה. אִי נָמֵי, בַּהֲדֵי דְּעָבֵיד עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ פַּסְקֵיהּ מָרָא לְשָׁקֵיהּ וּמִית, דְּלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ שְׁהוּת בִּימָמָא דִּלְכַפַּר לֵיהּ.

a23.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים אַף הַמְגַדֵּף כּוּ׳. מַאי אַף הַמְגַדֵּף שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה?

a24.he: רַבָּנַן שְׁמַעוּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּתָנֵי בַּעַל אוֹב וְלָא תָּנֵי יִדְּעוֹנִי, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא דְּלָא מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן, מִשּׁוּם דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה? מְגַדֵּף נָמֵי לֵית בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה!

a25.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְגַדֵּף מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן, הוֹאִיל וְנֶאֱמַר בּוֹ כָּרֵת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וְאוֹמֵר: ״וְנָשָׂא חֶטְאוֹ״. וּכְלָלָא הוּא, כֹּל הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ כָּרֵת מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן? וְהָא פֶּסַח וּמִילָה דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ כָּרֵת וְלָא מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן!

b1.he: הָכִי קָאָמַר: מְגַדֵּף מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן הוֹאִיל וּבָא בּוֹ כָּרֵת בִּמְקוֹם קׇרְבָּן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא. קָסָבַר: מִיגּוֹ דְּבָעֵי מִכְתַּב כָּרֵת בְּעָלְמָא, וּכְתִיב כָּרֵת בִּמְקוֹם קׇרְבָּן, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן.

b2.he: וְאוֹמֵר: ״חֶטְאוֹ יִשָּׂא״. אֲתָא[ן] לְרַבָּנַן, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבָּנַן: אָמְרִיתוּ מְגַדֵּף לֵית בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה, מַהוּ מְגַדֵּף – מְבָרֵךְ אֶת הַשֵּׁם. אֶלָּא כָּרֵת דִּכְתִיב, לְמַאי אֲתָא?

b3.he: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: לִיתֵּן כָּרֵת לִמְקַלֵּל, דִּכְתִיב בִּמְקַלֵּל: (״חֶטְאוֹ יִשָּׂא הָאִישׁ הַהוּא״) [״וְנָשָׂא חֶטְאוֹ״], וּכְתִיב בְּפֶסַח שֵׁנִי: ״חֶטְאוֹ יִשָּׂא״, מָה לְהַלָּן – כָּרֵת, אַף כָּאן – כָּרֵת.

b4.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אֶת ה׳ [הוּא] מְגַדֵּף״, אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כְּאָדָם הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ ״גֵּירַפְתָּה הַקְּעָרָה וְחִיסַּרְתָּהּ״. קָסָבַר: מְגַדֵּף – מְבָרֵךְ אֶת הַשֵּׁם הוּא.

b5.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: כְּאָדָם הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ ״גֵּירַפְתָּה הַקְּעָרָה וְלֹא חִיסַּרְתָּהּ״. קָסָבַר: מְגַדֵּף – הַיְינוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.

b6.he: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: ״אֶת ה׳״, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: בְּעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא בָּא הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא לִיתֵּן כָּרֵת לִמְבָרֵךְ הַשֵּׁם.

b7.he: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ מְבִיאוֹת קׇרְבָּן וְנֶאֱכָל, וְיֵשׁ מְבִיאוֹת קׇרְבָּן וְאֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל, וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאֵינָם מְבִיאוֹת.

b8.he: מְבִיאוֹת קׇרְבָּן וְנֶאֱכָל: הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין בְּהֵמָה חַיָּה וָעוֹף, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ מִצּוּרַת אָדָם.

b9.he: הַמַּפֶּלֶת סַנְדָּל אוֹ שִׁילְיָא אוֹ שַׁפִּיר מְרוּקָּם, וְהַיּוֹצֵא מְחוּתָּךְ, וְכֵן שִׁפְחָה שֶׁהִפִּילָה, מְבִיאָה קׇרְבָּן וְנֶאֱכָל.

b10.he: וְאֵלּוּ מְבִיאוֹת וְאֵינָן נֶאֱכָלוֹת: הַמַּפֶּלֶת וְאֵין יוֹדֵעַ מָה הִפִּילָה, וּשְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֶׁהִפִּילוּ, אַחַת מִמִּין פְּטוּר וְאַחַת מִמִּין חוֹבָה. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֵימָתַי? בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָלְכוּ זֶה לַמִּזְרָח וְזֶה לַמַּעֲרָב. אֲבָל אִם הָיוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶן עוֹמְדוֹת – שְׁתֵּיהֶן מְבִיאוֹת קׇרְבָּן, וְנֶאֱכָל.

b11.he: אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין מְבִיאוֹת: הַמַּפֶּלֶת שַׁפִּיר מָלֵא מַיִם, מָלֵא דָּם, מָלֵא גְּנִינִים, הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין דָּגִים וַחֲגָבִים וּשְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים, הַמַּפֶּלֶת יוֹם אַרְבָּעִים, וְיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְחַיֵּיב בְּיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן.

b12.he: גְּמָ׳ שִׁפְחָה מְנָלַן? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, גִּיּוֹרֶת וְשִׁפְחָה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִשָּׁה״.

b13.he: מַאי ״וְכֵן שִׁפְחָה״? סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: כִּי אָמְרִינַן כׇּל מִצְוָה שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה חַיֶּיבֶת בָּהּ – עֶבֶד חַיָּיב בָּהּ, הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּדָבָר שֶׁשָּׁוֶה בֵּין אִישׁ וּבֵין אִשָּׁה. אֲבָל יוֹלֶדֶת, דִּבְנָשִׁים אִיתַהּ, בַּאֲנָשִׁים לֵיתַהּ, אֵימָא לָא תִּחַיַּיב שִׁפְחָה, אַהָכִי תְּנָא: שִׁפְחָה.

b14.he: אֵלּוּ מְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן כּוּ׳. מַאי עָבְדִין? מַייתְיָן תַּרְוַיְיהוּ חַד קׇרְבָּן וַדַּאי, וְחַטַּאת עוֹף סָפֵק, וּמַתְנֵי.

b15.he: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי תְּנָאָה? וְהָתְנַן: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מְבִיאוֹת שְׁנֵיהֶן חַטָּאת אַחַת. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר אֵין שְׁנֵיהֶן מְבִיאוֹת חַטָּאת אַחַת. אַלְמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֵית לֵיהּ תְּנָאָה!

b16.he: אָמַר רָבָא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בִּמְחוּסַּר כַּפָּרָה. וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בִּמְחוּסַּר כַּפָּרָה.

b17.he: מַאי טַעְמָא? הָתָם בָּעֵי גַּבְרָא יְדִיעָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״אוֹ הוֹדַע אֵלָיו חַטָּאתוֹ״ הִילְכָּךְ, לָא מַתְיָין וּמַתְנְיָ[ין]. אֲבָל הָכָא, כִּי מַתְיָין נָשִׁים קׇרְבָּן – לְאִישְׁתְּרוֹיֵי בַּאֲכִילַת קָדָשִׁים.

b18.he: כִּדְתָנֵי סֵיפָא דְּהַהִיא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל חַטָּאת שֶׁהִיא בָּאָה עַל חֵטְא – אֵין שְׁתַּיִם מְבִיאוֹת אוֹתָהּ.

b19.he: אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין מְבִיאוֹת כּוּ׳ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְחַיֵּיב בְּיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן. מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן? אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִם נְקֵבָה תֵּלֵד״, לְרַבּוֹת לֵידָה אַחֶרֶת, מַאי הִיא – יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן.

b20.he: וְרַבָּנַן מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַבִּי מַנִּי בַּר פַּטִּישׁ: ״אִשָּׁה כִּי תַזְרִיעַ וְיָלְדָה״ – עַד שֶׁתֵּלֵד מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁמַּזְרַעַת.

b21.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּפֶּלֶת לְאוֹר שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹטְרִין מִן הַקׇּרְבָּן, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְחַיְּיבִין.

b22.he: אָמְרוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי: מַאי שְׁנָא אוֹר שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד מִיּוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד? אִם שָׁיוָה לוֹ לְטוּמְאָה, לֹא יִשְׁוֶה לוֹ לְקׇרְבָּן?

b23.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּמַפֶּלֶת יוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד, שֶׁכֵּן יָצְאָה לְשָׁעָה שֶׁהִיא רְאוּיָה לְהָבִיא בָּהּ קׇרְבָּן, תֹּאמַר בְּמַפֶּלֶת לְאוֹר שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד, שֶׁלֹּא יָצְאָה לְשָׁעָה שֶׁהִיא רְאוּיָה לְהָבִיא בָּהּ קׇרְבָּן.

b24.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל: וַהֲלֹא הַמַּפֶּלֶת יוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת תּוֹכִיחַ, שֶׁלֹּא יָצְאָה לְשָׁעָה שֶׁהִיא רְאוּיָה לְהָבִיא בָּהּ קׇרְבָּן, וְחַיֶּיבֶת קׇרְבָּן!

b25.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם יוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת, שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לְקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד, רָאוּי לְקׇרְבַּן צִיבּוּר, תֹּאמַר בְּמַפֶּלֶת לְאוֹר שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם וְאֶחָד, שֶׁאֵין הַלַּיְלָה רָאוּי לֹא לְקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד וְלֹא לְקׇרְבַּן צִיבּוּר?

b26.he: וְהַדָּמִים אֵינָן מוֹכִיחִים, שֶׁהַמַּפֶּלֶת בְּתוֹךְ מְלֹאת – דָּמֶיהָ טְמֵאִים, וּפְטוּרָה מִן הַקׇּרְבָּן.

messages.text: 7a

Continued from 6b: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda disagreed whether a king or priest who was already anointed counts as a “stranger” for the anointing oil, and Rav Ika, son of Rav Ami, said that each follows his own line of reasoning, as taught in a mishna (Terumot 7:2):

With regard to the daughter of a priest who married an Israelite and then unwittingly partook of teruma, she pays the principal, as a thief would, as she partook of teruma to which she owns no rights. But she does not pay the additional one-fifth payment, which is the fine paid by an Israelite who partakes of teruma unwittingly (see Leviticus 22:14).

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יֹאכַל קֹדֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָה וְיָסַף חֲמִשִׁיתוֹ עָלָיו וְנָתַן לַכֹּהֵן אֶת־הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: but if someone eats of a sacred donation unwittingly, the priest shall be paid for the sacred donation, adding one-fifth of its value.

notes.he: דלא זרה שהרי לא נתחללה שאם ימות בעלה ותנשא לכהן אוכלת או אם זרע אין לה הדרא לתרומה:
notes.en: Who married an Israelite … and she does not pay the fifth: for she is not a stranger [zara], since she has not been profaned: if her husband dies and she marries a priest, she eats [teruma]; or if she has no offspring, she returns to teruma.

notes.he: אשם ל"ג:
notes.en: She pays, etc.: [the word] “guilt offering” is not part of our reading.

messages.text: This is because she is not completely disqualified from the priesthood, since if she becomes widowed or divorced without having borne children she will again be permitted to partake of teruma. And if she commits adultery her death penalty is administered by burning, as is the halakha with regard to the daughter of a priest (see Leviticus 21:9).

notes.he: אין דינה ליכל בתרומה ואם אכלה משלמת את הקרן ואינה משלמת את החומש דאין דינה כזרה גמורה שהרי אוכלת היא בתרומה בחוזרת אם תהיה אלמנה וגרושה וזרע אין לה ושבה אל בית אביה וכו' והואיל וכך מיתתה נמי בשרפה אם זינתה כדין בת כהן:
notes.en: [A printer’s marker here reads: “Up to here belongs to 6b.”] The daughter of a priest who married an Israelite: her law is not to eat teruma, and if she ate, she pays the principal but does not pay the fifth, since her law is not that of a complete stranger, for she does eat teruma if she returns, if she becomes a widow or divorcée and has no offspring and returns to her father’s house, etc. And since that is so, her death too is by burning if she commits adultery, according to the law of a priest’s daughter.

messages.text: By contrast, if she married one of those who are unfit for her to marry due to his lineage, thereby disqualifying herself from the priesthood for the future, she pays the principal and the additional one-fifth payment, and her death is by strangulation, as is the halakha with regard to Israelite women. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: ורבי מאיר לטעמיה דאע"ג דמעיקרא לאו זרה היא השתא מיהא זרה הויא:
notes.en: And her death is by strangulation: Rabbi Meir follows his own line of reasoning, that even though at the outset she was not a stranger, now at any rate she is a stranger.

notes.he: הואיל ונתחללה דינה כזרה בת ישראל:
notes.en: She married one of those unfit for her: since she has been profaned, her law is that of a stranger, an Israelite woman.

messages.text: In both this case and that case, whether she was married to an Israelite or to one unfit for her to marry, she pays the principal but she does not pay the additional one-fifth payment, and her death is by burning, as she previously had the status of a daughter of the priesthood.

notes.he: דבעינן זר מתחלתו:
notes.en: In both this case and that case, etc.: since we require one who is a stranger from the outset.

notes.dh: וחכ"א אחת זו ואחת זו כו'
notes.he: כלומר כיון דלא הויא זרה מתחילתה ועד סופה אינה משלמת את החומש ודינה כבת כהן והיינו ואזדו לטעמייהו:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: Both this and that, etc.: that is, since she is not a stranger from her beginning to her end, she does not pay the fifth, and her law is that of a priest’s daughter. And this is [what was meant by]: and they follow their lines of reasoning.

messages.text: This opinion of the Rabbis is presumably that of Rabbi Yehuda, who is usually the disputant of Rabbi Meir. As explained with regard to the anointing of a king, Rabbi Yehuda requires that the individual in question must have the status of a stranger, i.e., not a High Priest or a king, from beginning to end.

notes.he: היינו רבי יהודה בר פלוגתיה:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: this is Rabbi Yehuda, his [Rabbi Meir’s] disputant.

messages.text: The dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda applies to the placing of the anointing oil, and it is explained by those answers that we answered earlier, that according to Rabbi Meir one is liable for the placing of any amount, as the verse uses an expression of applying, whereas according to Rabbi Yehuda one is liable only if one places oil that is the volume of an olive-bulk.

notes.he: דטעמיה דר"מ משום דאיתקש לסיכה:
notes.en: And by those answers that we answered: that Rabbi Meir’s reason is that [placing] is juxtaposed with applying.

messages.text: But with regard to placing in general, e.g., the prohibition not to place frankincense on the meal offering of a sinner (see Leviticus 5:11), everyone agrees one is liable for placing only the volume of an olive-bulk.

notes.he: כגון לא יתן עליה לבונה דמנחת חוטא בכזית דילפינן מונתן לכהן את הקדש (ויקרא כ״ב:י״ד) והכי מפרשא בפרק כל המנחות באות מצה (מנחות נט:):
notes.en: But placing in general: for example, “he shall not put frankincense on it” [Leviticus 5:11], said of the meal offering of a sinner, [is] with an olive-bulk, which we derive from “and he shall give to the priest the sacred item” (Leviticus 22:14). And so it is explained in the chapter Kol HaMenaḥot Baot Matza (Menaḥot 59b).

notes.he: באותה נתינה דשמן המשחה וכי שינוייא דשנינן דר' מאיר דיליף מעל בשר אדם לא ייסך ור' יהודה יליף מנתינה דעלמא אבל כל נתינה דעלמא דברי הכל בכזית:
notes.en: The dispute: concerning that placing of the anointing oil, and according to the answers that we answered: that Rabbi Meir derives from “upon the flesh of a person it shall not be applied” and Rabbi Yehuda derives from giving in general. But with regard to all giving in general, everyone agrees [that it is] with an olive-bulk.

messages.text: Anyone included in the obligation not to apply anointing oil to himself or others is likewise included as the object of: It shall not be applied, i.e., it is prohibited to apply the oil to him. And anyone not included in the obligation not to apply anointing oil to himself or others is not included as the object of: It shall not be applied.
messages.lead: § The Gemara discusses the matter itself: A tanna teaches a baraita before Rabbi Elazar:

messages.text: You are saying well, as it is written: “Upon the flesh of a person it shall not be applied [lo yisakh]” (Exodus 30:32), and you read into the verse: Lo yasikh, he shall not apply it to others. This dual reading indicates that one who is commanded not to apply the oil is the same as the one upon whom it is prohibited to apply the oil, as stated by the tanna.
messages.quote: Anyone included in the obligation not to apply anointing oil … is likewise included

verse.he: עַל־בְּשַׂר אָדָם לֹא יִיסָךְ וּבְמַתְכֻּנְתּוֹ לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ כָּמֹהוּ קֹדֶשׁ הוּא קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיֶה לָכֶם׃
verse.en: It must not be rubbed on any person’s body, and you must not make anything like it in the same proportions; it is sacred, to be held sacred by you.

notes.he: בשני יודין שדי חדא לתוך התיבה וקרי לא יסיך דמשמע מי שמצווה שלא יסיך לא לעצמו ולא לאחרים מצווה אחר עליו שלא לסוכו ועובד כוכבים לאו בר מצוה הוא:
notes.en: It is written lo yisakh: with two letters yod. Put one of them inside the word and read lo yasikh, which means: one who is commanded not to apply [the oil], neither to himself nor to others, is the one whom another is commanded not to anoint. And a gentile is not subject to the commandment.

notes.he: ואפי' מאן דלית ליה מסורת בעלמא הכא אינו מוסיף על התיבה אלא מסרס התיבה להטיל יו"ד בין סמ"ך לכ"ף:
notes.en: Read into it lo yasikh: Even according to one who does not hold that the traditional reading [masoret] is authoritative elsewhere, here it does not add to the word but only rearranges the word, placing a yod between the samekh and the khaf.

notes.dh: שפיר קא אמרת לא ייסך כתיב
notes.he: ויכול אתה לדורשו בלא ייסוך ובלא יסיך:
notes.en: You are saying well, it is written lo yisakh: and you can expound it both as “it shall not be applied” and as “he shall not apply.”

messages.text: From where is it derived with regard to a High Priest who took from the anointing oil that is on his head and placed it on his stomach; from where is it derived that he is liable? It is derived from a verse, as it is stated: “Upon the flesh of a person it shall not be applied” (Exodus 30:32).

notes.dh: מנין לכ"ג שנטל משמן המשחה כו'
notes.he: תימה אמאי לא קאמר לעיל דהוי שמן המשחה שני כתובים הבאים כאחד וי"ל דלא חשיב נעשית מצוותו אלא לאחר שניגב השמן כדמסיק שמן משחת אלהיו עליו איקרי אע"ג דאית עליו לא איתחיל:
notes.en: From where with regard to a High Priest who took from the anointing oil, etc.: It is puzzling: why was it not said above that the anointing oil is [a case of] two verses that come as one [and so teach nothing beyond themselves]? One can say that its mitzva is not regarded as completed until the oil has been wiped off, as is concluded: it is called “the anointing oil of his God is upon him”; even though it is upon him, it has not been profaned.

messages.text: @Rav Ashi What is different between this case and that which is taught in a baraita: In the case of a priest who applied teruma oil to himself, the Israelite son of his daughter may rub against [mitaggel] this oil without concern that he might be deriving benefit from teruma?
messages.quote: a High Priest who took from the anointing oil that is on his head and placed it on his stomach

notes.dh: כהן שסך בן בתו ישראל מתעגל בו כו'
notes.he: ופי' כהן שסך את עצמו שמן יכול בן בתו ישראל לבא להתעגל בו ואפילו גדול ושף עצמו באבי אמו ואינו חושש אלמא כיון דבטלה בהתירא בטלה והכי תניא בהדיא בתוספתא דמסכת תרומות (פ"י ה"י) סך כהן את עצמו שמן של תרומה ומביא בן בתו ישראל ומעגלו על גביו. ובן בתו ישראל דנקט משום דרגיל אצלו והוא הדין לאחריני:
notes.en: A priest who applied [teruma oil], the Israelite son of his daughter may rub against it, etc.: The explanation is: a priest who applied teruma oil to himself, his Israelite daughter’s son may come and roll in it; and even if he is an adult and rubs himself against his mother’s father, he need not be concerned. Evidently, once it has been used up in a permitted way, it is used up. And so it is taught explicitly in the Tosefta of tractate Terumot (10:10): A priest applied teruma oil to himself, and he brings his Israelite daughter’s son and rolls him over himself. And it mentions the Israelite son of his daughter because he is regularly with him; the same applies to others.

notes.he: כהן שסך שמן של תרומה בן בתו ישראל שאינו רשאי לסוכו ואעפ"כ מתעגל בו אותו בן בתו ישראל מתהפך בו באותו שמן כדי שימשח כל גופו ואינו חושש לשם איסור הואיל והוא לא שם על עצמו קודם לכן באיסור:
notes.en: A priest who applied teruma oil: his Israelite daughter’s son, who is not permitted to apply it, nevertheless rolls in it: that Israelite daughter’s son turns over in that oil so as to anoint his whole body, and he need not be concerned about a prohibition, since he did not put it on himself beforehand in a prohibited way.

messages.text: There, with regard to teruma oil, it is written: “They will die through it if they profane it” (Leviticus 22:9), and since the priest has already profaned the oil by using it, it is considered profaned.
messages.quote: the Israelite son of his daughter may rub against this oil without concern

verse.he: וְשָׁמְרוּ אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתִּי וְלֹא־יִשְׂאוּ עָלָיו חֵטְא וּמֵתוּ בוֹ כִּי יְחַלְּלֻהוּ אֲנִי יְהֹוָה מְקַדְּשָׁם׃
verse.en: They shall keep My charge, lest they incur guilt thereby and die for it, having committed profanation: I GOD consecrate them.

messages.text: But with regard to the anointing oil it is written: “For the consecration of the anointing oil of His God is upon him” (Leviticus 21:12). The Merciful One calls it anointing oil even at this stage, to teach that even though it is upon the High Priest it is not considered profaned, and instead remains sacred.

verse.he: וּמִן־הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא יֵצֵא וְלֹא יְחַלֵּל אֵת מִקְדַּשׁ אֱלֹהָיו כִּי נֵזֶר שֶׁמֶן מִשְׁחַת אֱלֹהָיו עָלָיו אֲנִי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: He shall not go outside the sanctuary and profane the sanctuary of his God, for upon him is the distinction of the anointing oil of Mine, the ETERNAL’s.

notes.he: לא דמי התם בשמן של תרומה ומתו בו כי יחללוהו הוא הכהן שסכו ענוש שחיללו וכיון שחיללו יצא לחולין הילכך מתעגל בו ואינו חושש הכא אע"ג דאיתא עליו לא איתחל דהא נמשח ראשו בהיתר וכיון דלא איתחל הילכך כי סכו על בני מעיו חייב:
notes.en: He said to him: It is not comparable. There, with teruma oil, [it is written] “They will die through it if they profane it”: the priest who applied it is the one punished for having profaned it, and once he has profaned it, it has gone out to non-sacred status; therefore [the grandson] rolls in it without concern. Here, even though it is upon him, it is not profaned, for his head was anointed in a permitted way; and since it is not profaned, when he applies it to his stomach he is liable.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: For any of these prohibitions, one is liable to receive karet for its intentional violation and to bring a sin offering for its unwitting violation. And for violation in a case where it is unknown to him whether he transgressed, he is liable to bring a provisional guilt offering.

The Gemara notes that the mishna further teaches: This is the halakha for all the transgressions listed above except for one who defiles the Temple, i.e., he enters the Temple while ritually impure or renders its consecrated items ritually impure. The Gemara asks: From what halakha does the tanna exclude these cases? After all, one who enters the Temple while impure or renders its consecrated items impure is also liable to receive karet.
The Gemara answers: This is what the mishna is teaching: Except for one who defiles the Temple or renders its consecrated items ritually impure, as he does not bring a provisional guilt offering.

notes.he: שאין אשם תלוי בא אלא על ספק חטאת קבועה כדמפרש בפ' בתרא (לקמן כריתות כה.):
notes.en: As he does not bring a provisional guilt offering: for a provisional guilt offering comes only for an uncertain [liability to a] fixed sin offering, as is explained in the last chapter (below, Keritot 25a).

notes.he: דקתני חוץ והלא חייב נמי בזדון כרת ובשוגג חטאת דקרבן עולה ויורד היינו חטאת. האי חוץ דקתני למעוטי מטומאת מקדש וקדשיו על לא הודע שלו מאשם תלוי דמי שחטאתו בקבועה מביא אשם תלוי ולא מי שמביא קרבן עולה ויורד א"כ כיון דלמעוטי מאשם תלוי קתני חוץ וניתני נמי ממי שעבר עליו יום הכפורים אחר שבא אותו ספק חטאת לידו אינו מביא אשם תלוי שכיפר עליו יום הכפורים:
notes.en: From what does it exclude it? For it teaches “except,” but is he not also liable to karet for the intentional [act] and to a sin offering for the unwitting one? For a sliding-scale offering is a sin offering. This “except” that it teaches is to exclude [one who defiles] the Temple and its consecrated items, in a case where it is unknown to him, from a provisional guilt offering; for one whose sin offering is fixed brings a provisional guilt offering, but not one who brings a sliding-scale offering. If so, since it teaches “except” to exclude from a provisional guilt offering, let it also teach [the exclusion of] one over whom Yom Kippur passed after that uncertain sin offering came into his hands, who does not bring a provisional guilt offering, because Yom Kippur atoned for him.

messages.text: The Gemara suggests: And let the mishna also teach: Except for one who sinned and Yom Kippur passed, as he too does not bring a provisional guilt offering.

When the tanna teaches these exceptions he is referring to those cases where there is a sin and nevertheless the Merciful One exempts him from bringing a provisional guilt offering. By contrast, in a case where Yom Kippur passed, there is no remaining sin, as Yom Kippur atoned for him, i.e., for his sin.
messages.quote: Except for one who sinned and Yom Kippur passed

notes.he: חוץ מידי דאתיא ליה לספק חטאיה ורחמנא פטריה מאשם תלוי משום דאין חטאתו קבועה אבל דעבר עליו יוה"כ לא איתיה לחטאיה הילכך לא קתני:
notes.en: Reish Lakish said: When it teaches “except,” [it means] a case where his uncertain sin is there and the Merciful One exempts him from a provisional guilt offering, because his sin offering is not fixed. But one over whom Yom Kippur passed has no sin remaining; therefore it is not taught.

messages.text: The mishna is referring to one who rejects the atonement of Yom Kippur, who says: Yom Kippur does not atone for one’s sins. In this situation Yom Kippur does not atone for him, which means that if he retracted from his sinful ways after Yom Kippur he is required to bring a provisional guilt offering. Therefore, it cannot be listed in the exceptions stated in the mishna.
messages.quote: Except for one who sinned and Yom Kippur passed

notes.he: ביוה"כ דאמר לא תכפר עליו משום הכי לא תני ליה:
notes.en: The mishna is referring to one who rejects: Yom Kippur, who said that it should not atone for him. For this reason [the mishna] does not teach it.

notes.he: היינו טעמא דלא תנא חוץ ממי שעבר עליו יוה"כ במבעיט יוה"כ דקאמר דלא ניכפר עליה יוה"כ דאי הדר ביה בתר יוה"כ דבעי לאייתויי קרבן מחייב לאייתויי אשם תלוי דהא לא כיפר עליו יוה"כ דבעט בו וכיון דחייב באשם תלוי במבעט משום הכי לא תנייה:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: This is the reason it does not teach “except for one over whom Yom Kippur passed”: [it speaks] of one who rejects Yom Kippur, who says that Yom Kippur should not atone for him. For if he retracts after Yom Kippur and needs to bring an offering, he is obligated to bring a provisional guilt offering, since Yom Kippur did not atone for him, as he rejected it. And since one who rejects is obligated to bring a provisional guilt offering, it is therefore not taught.

messages.text: The Gemara notes: And Reish Lakish does not explain the mishna in this manner, as he maintains that even with regard to one who rejects its atonement, Yom Kippur atones for his sins.

notes.he: וריש לקיש סבר אי לאו משום טעמא דידי משום מבעט נמי מיפטר דהא כיפר עליה:
notes.en: And Reish Lakish holds: [even] apart from my reason, one who rejects is also exempt, for [Yom Kippur] atoned for him.

messages.text: The Gemara notes: And their dispute is with regard to the issue that is the subject of the dispute between later amora’im: Concerning one who says: My sin offering, which is sacrificed for me, should not atone for me,

notes.he: פי' כי היכי דפליגי ר"י ור"ל במבעט בי"כ ה"נ פליגי אביי ורבא במבעט בחטאת לא בעי למימר דרבי יוחנן ור"ל פליגי נמי במבעט בחטאת כמו במבעט ביום הכיפורים דאיכא למימר עד כאן לא אמר ר"ל אלא ביום הכיפורים שמכפר על המזיד כשוגג ואי הוה פליגי אביי ורבא נמי ביה"כ א"כ כי הדר ביה רבא ה"מ דהדר ביה מחטאת אבל מיה"כ לא הדר ביה וסבר כר"ל וכאידך ברייתא דיה"כ הוא מ"מ וא"כ קשה הילכתא אהילכתא דקי"ל כרבי יוחנן לגבי ר"ל וקי"ל כרבא לגבי אביי אלא נראה דלא פליגי ביה"כ ועוד דסבירא לן כרבנן דפליגי ארבי ואמרי דיה"כ לא מכפר אלא על השבין דהילכתא כרבי מחבירו ולא מחביריו. והדר ביה רבא מהא דתניא כו'. דליכא למימר דלא שמיע ליה ברייתא דהא לקמן מתרץ לה:
notes.en: And in the dispute: That is, just as Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish disagree about one who rejects Yom Kippur, so too Abaye and Rava disagree about one who rejects a sin offering. It does not mean to say that Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish also disagree about one who rejects a sin offering as they do about one who rejects Yom Kippur, for one can say that Reish Lakish said his view only with regard to Yom Kippur, which atones for the intentional as for the unwitting. And if Abaye and Rava also disagreed about Yom Kippur, then when Rava retracted, he would have retracted only with regard to a sin offering, but with regard to Yom Kippur he would not have retracted, and would hold like Reish Lakish and like the other baraita about Yom Kippur, [that it atones] in any case. If so, one halakha would be difficult against another, since we hold like Rabbi Yoḥanan against Reish Lakish and we hold like Rava against Abaye. Rather, it appears that they do not disagree about Yom Kippur. Moreover, we hold like the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi and say that Yom Kippur atones only for those who repent, since the halakha follows Rabbi against his colleague but not against his colleagues. And Rava retracted because of that which is taught, etc.: for one cannot say that he had not heard the baraita, since below he resolves it.

notes.he: אביי כר' יוחנן ורבא כר"ל:
notes.en: And in the dispute: Abaye is like Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rava is like Reish Lakish.

messages.text: This sin offering does not atone for him.
It atones for him.

The Gemara explains: In a case where he said: I do not want it to be sacrificed, everyone agrees that it does not atone for him, as it is written: “He shall bring it in accordance with his will” (Leviticus 1:3), which indicates that if the offering is brought against his will it is not effective. Where they disagree is when he says: The sin offering should be sacrificed but it should not atone for me.

verse.he: אִם־עֹלָה קׇרְבָּנוֹ מִן־הַבָּקָר זָכָר תָּמִים יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד יַקְרִיב אֹתוֹ לִרְצֹנוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: If your offering is a burnt offering from the herd, you shall make your offering a male without blemish. You shall bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, for acceptance in your behalf before GOD.

messages.text: It does not atone for him, as he said that it should not atone for him.
It does atone for him, as once he says it should be sacrificed, the atonement comes by itself.
The Gemara notes: And Rava retracted his opinion, as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: שלא יכפר:
notes.en: And there is a logical inference: that it should not atone.

messages.text: One might have thought that Yom Kippur atones for those who repent and for those who do not repent.

And there is a logical inference to negate this assertion: Just as a sin offering and a guilt offering atone, and likewise Yom Kippur atones, just as a sin offering and a guilt offering atone only for those who repent, so too, Yom Kippur atones only for those who repent.

notes.he: דלרצונו בעינן:
notes.en: Only for those who repent: since we require [the offering to be brought] in accordance with his will.

messages.text: No, if you said this is the halakha with regard to a sin offering and a guilt offering, which do not atone for intentional sins as they do for unwitting sins, shall you also say that this is the halakha with regard to Yom Kippur, which does atone for intentional sins as it does for unwitting sins? Yom Kippur effects atonement even in cases where offerings do not.

notes.he: אשם לאו דוקא נקט דהא אשכחן אשם אמזיד בפרק שני (לקמן כריתות ח:) ד' מביאין על הזדון:
notes.en: “Guilt offering” is not meant precisely, for we find a guilt offering for an intentional sin in the second chapter (below, Keritot 8b): four [people] bring [an offering] for an intentional [sin].

notes.dh: תאמר ביה"כ שמכפר על המזיד כו'
notes.he: תימה דלימא ד' דברים שמביאין על הזדון יוכיח שאין מכפרין אלא [על] השבים ואריב"ן דמה להנך שאין מכפרין על חייבי כריתות ועוד א"ר דנהי דיש חטאות מכפרין על המזיד מ"מ כמה חטאות אין מכפרין על המזיד משא"כ ביה"כ:
notes.en: Shall you say with regard to Yom Kippur, which atones for intentional sins, etc.: It is puzzling: let it say that the four [people] who bring [an offering] for an intentional [sin] will prove [the point], that they atone only for those who repent. And Rivan answered: What [comparison is there] with those, which do not atone for those liable to karet? And [our] teacher said further: Granted that there are sin offerings that atone for the intentional, nevertheless many sin offerings do not atone for the intentional, which is not so with Yom Kippur.

notes.he: תאמר ביוה"כ שמכפר על המזיד כשוגג כדכתיב והתודה עליו את כל עונות ב"י:
notes.en: Shall you say with regard to Yom Kippur, which atones for the intentional as for the unwitting: as it is written: “And confess over it all the iniquities of the children of Israel” [Leviticus 16:21].

messages.text: And since it is the case that the atonement of Yom Kippur is far-reaching in that it atones for intentional sins as it does for unwitting sins, it follows that it may atone both for those who repent and for those who do not repent. To dispel this notion, the verse states: “Yet on the tenth day of this month it is Yom Kippur” (Leviticus 23:27). By means of the word “yet,” the verse divided and limited the atonement of Yom Kippur so that it atones only for those who repent.

verse.he: אַךְ בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִי הַזֶּה יוֹם הַכִּפֻּרִים הוּא מִקְרָא־קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיֶה לָכֶם וְעִנִּיתֶם אֶת־נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם וְהִקְרַבְתֶּם אִשֶּׁה לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Mark, the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It shall be a sacred occasion for you: you shall practice self-denial, and you shall bring an offering by fire to GOD;

notes.he: בעשור לחדש יוה"כ הוא:
notes.en: “Yet”: “Yet on the tenth day of this month it is Yom Kippur.”

notes.he: יום כפור לשבין ולא לשאינן שבין:
notes.en: Divided: Yom Kippur [atones] for those who repent and not for those who do not repent.

messages.text: The Gemara analyzes this baraita. What is the meaning of: Those who repent and those who do not repent? Shall we say those who repent are those whose transgressions were unwitting, whereas those who do not repent are those whose transgressions were intentional?
messages.quote: Yom Kippur atones for those who repent and for those who do not repent

notes.he: דקתני אין מכפרין אלא על השבין:
notes.en: What [is the meaning of] those who repent: that it teaches: they atone only for those who repent.

messages.text: This cannot be the case, as the baraita teaches: No, if you said this is the halakha with regard to a sin offering and a guilt offering, which do not atone for intentional sins as they do for unwitting sins. Since the baraita is referring to the concepts of intentional and unwitting sins in this clause, the categories of those who repent and do not repent must have another meaning.

notes.dh: הא קתני לא אם אמרת כו'
notes.he: וא"כ מאי קאמר היינו הך:
notes.en: But it teaches: No, if you said, etc.: and if so, what is it saying? That is the same point.

notes.dh: אי נימא שבין שוגג ושאינן שבין מזיד
notes.he: שלא שב מידיעתו הא קתני לא אם אמרת בחטאת ואשם שאין מכפר על המזיד כשוגג היינו הא ומאי קא מהדר ליה:
notes.en: If you say that those who repent are the unwitting and those who do not repent are the intentional, who did not turn back from his knowledge — but it teaches: No, if you said with regard to a sin offering and a guilt offering, which do not atone for the intentional as for the unwitting; that is the same thing, and what is it answering him?

messages.text: If one unwittingly ate forbidden fat and separated an offering for this sin, and became an apostate and subsequently retracted his apostasy, nevertheless, since the offering was rejected from being sacrificed while he was an apostate, it shall remain rejected.
messages.lead: Rather, the category of those who do not repent is like that which Ulla says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

notes.he: והיינו דקאמר חטאת אינו מכפר אלא על השבין ששבין משעת הפרשה עד שעת הקרבה ולא שהמיר דתו בינתיים והתם בעי למילף יוה"כ דאם המיר דת קודם יוה"כ וחזר בו אחר יוה"כ תו לא מכפר עליה יום הכפורים אחר על עבירותיו שמקמי המרתו:
notes.en: Rather, like this [statement], etc.: and this is what it is saying: a sin offering atones only for those who repent, who are repentant from the time of designation until the time of sacrifice, and not for one who became an apostate in the interim. And there it wishes to derive [the same for] Yom Kippur: that if he became an apostate before Yom Kippur and retracted after Yom Kippur, another Yom Kippur will no longer atone for him for his transgressions from before his apostasy.

notes.he: אע"ג דקי"ל כל שבידו לא הוי דיחוי ה"מ שאינו נדחה מחמת פסולו כמו שקיבל הדם ונתנו לשמאלו דהוי כאילו נתנו על הרצפה שיחזור ויטלנו אבל האי נדחה מחמת פסול הגוף ודמי לדאמרינן בזבחים מזבח שנפגם כל קדשים שהיו שם פסולים אע"ג דבידו למלאות הפגימה:
notes.en: Since it was rejected, it shall remain rejected: Even though we hold that whatever is in one’s power [to remedy] is not rejection, that applies where it is not rejected because of a disqualification of its own, as when one received the blood and put it into his left hand, which is like having put it on the floor, where he can go back and take it. But this one is rejected because of a disqualification inherent in the person, and it is similar to what we say in Zevaḥim: if the altar was damaged, all the consecrated items that were there are disqualified, even though it is in one’s power to fill in the damage.

notes.he: מאי על שאינן שבין דלא מכפר דכתב אך חלק כי הא דאמר עולא אכל חלב והפריש קרבן ונשתמד קודם שהקריבו ואח"כ חזר בו בתשובה הואיל ונדחה קרבנו כי דלא שב מידיעתו נשתמד ידחה והיינו שאינן שבין נשתמד דלא מכפר עליה קרבנו:
notes.en: Rather: what are those who do not repent, for whom it does not atone, since it is written “yet,” dividing? Like that which Ulla said: He ate forbidden fat and designated an offering, and became an apostate before he sacrificed it, and afterward retracted in repentance: since his offering was rejected, as one who did not turn back from his knowledge when he became an apostate, it shall remain rejected. And this is [the meaning of] those who do not repent: one who became an apostate, for whom his offering does not atone.

messages.text: Accordingly, the baraita is suggesting that the same applies to one who became an apostate and Yom Kippur passed: Even if he retracts his apostasy, the following Yom Kippur should not atone for his transgression.

The Gemara rejects this interpretation: Granted, the offering is rejected from the altar, and therefore it cannot be sacrificed at a later stage. But the man himself is fit for atonement, and he can bring another sin offering.

notes.he: דבקרבן אמרינן הואיל ונדחה לאחר הפרשה ידחה מעל המזבח אבל גברא לגבי יוה"כ בר כפרה הוא כישראל מעליא:
notes.en: Why? Granted: that with regard to an offering we say that since it was rejected after its designation it is rejected from the altar; but the man, with regard to Yom Kippur, is fit for atonement, like a proper Jew.

notes.he: וקא מותיב אמאי קרי ליה שאינן שבין נהי דאידחי קרבן דידיה כיון דמשתמד אבל כיון דחזר בו גברא בר כפרה הוא:
notes.en: And he objects: Why call him one who does not repent? Granted that his offering was rejected, since he became an apostate; but since he retracted, the man is fit for atonement.

messages.text: The Gemara suggests another interpretation of the baraita: Rather, it must be that the category of those who repent is referring to one who says: My sin offering should atone for me, and the category of those who do not repent is referring to one who says: My sin offering should not atone for me.

The Gemara comments: Conclude from the baraita that a sin offering does not atone for one who states beforehand: My sin offering should not atone for me, in contradiction of the earlier statement of Rava. Since Rava was aware of this baraita, he must have retracted his opinion.

notes.he: לאו שבין דאמר תכפר עליה חטאתי שאינן שבין דמבעט דאמר לא תכפר עליה חטאתי וקאמר אך חלק אלמא הדר ביה רבא מדתניא:
notes.en: Rather: is it not that those who repent are one who says “Let my sin offering atone for me,” and those who do not repent are one who rejects, who says “My sin offering should not atone for me,” and it says “yet,” dividing? Evidently Rava retracted, because of what is taught.

messages.text: The Gemara continues its analysis of this baraita by comparing it to another baraita. And the Sages raise a contradiction:

notes.he: אהא דתני לעיל יוה"כ אינו מכפר אלא על השבין:
notes.en: And they raise a contradiction: against that which was taught above, that Yom Kippur atones only for those who repent.

notes.he: דלא כהא דקתני דאינן מכפרין על שאינן שבין:
notes.en: And they raise a contradiction: unlike that which is taught, that they do not atone for those who do not repent.

messages.text: One might have thought that Yom Kippur shall atone only for one who fasted on it and did not perform labor on it and declared it a holy convocation. With regard to one who did not fast on it, or performed labor on it, or did not declare it a holy convocation, one might have thought that Yom Kippur shall not atone for him.

notes.he: בתקון סדר התפלה:
notes.en: Declared it a holy convocation: by arranging the order of prayer.

notes.he: פי' בכסות נקייה כדאמר במכילתא מקרא קדש וכו':
notes.en: And declared it a holy convocation: that is, with clean clothing, as it says in the Mekhilta: “A holy convocation,” etc.

notes.he: וקראו מקרא קודש בברכות ובתפלות:
notes.en: And declared it a holy convocation: with blessings and prayers.

messages.text: To counter this the verse states: “Yet on the tenth day of this seventh month it is Yom Kippur” (Leviticus 23:27); the additional emphasis of “it is” serves to teach that the day atones in any case.

The ruling of this baraita disputes the one cited earlier, which states that Yom Kippur atones only for those who repent, and both are unattributed baraitot in the Sifra. They are difficult, as they contradict each other.

notes.he: הנך ברייתות:
notes.en: And both: these baraitot.

notes.he: סתם סיפרא ר' יהודה:
notes.en: An unattributed Sifra is Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: This is not difficult. This first baraita is the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, and that second baraita is the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi in accordance with his own opinion.

notes.he: ה"ג לא קשיא הא ר' יהודה הא רבי:
notes.en: This is the reading: “It is not difficult: this is Rabbi Yehuda and this is Rabbi.” [Rashi’s text names Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi directly, without “Rabbi in accordance with”.]

notes.he: דקתני כי יום כפורים הוא מכל מקום היינו ר' אליבא דידיה:
notes.en: That: which teaches “for it is Yom Kippur,” in any case, is Rabbi according to his own view.

messages.text: For all transgressions that are stated in the Torah, whether one repented or whether one did not repent, Yom Kippur atones.
messages.lead: As it is taught in a baraita that

messages.text: This is the halakha except for one who divests himself of the yoke of God, by denying His existence, and one who impudently reveals facets of the Torah in a manner that departs from their true meaning, and one who nullifies the covenant of the flesh, i.e., circumcision. With regard to these, if one repented, Yom Kippur atones, and if not, Yom Kippur does not atone.

notes.he: של כל המצות:
notes.en: Divests the yoke: of all the mitzvot.

notes.he: דורש באגדות של דופי כגון מנשה שהיה אומר מה היה לו למשה לומר ותמנע היתה פילגש:
notes.en: Reveals facets: expounds aggadot of scorn, like Manasseh, who would say: Why did Moses need to say, “And Timna was a concubine” [Genesis 36:12]?

messages.text: This indicates that according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, Yom Kippur atones even if one did not repent.

Both this baraita and that baraita are the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi in accordance with his own opinion, that Yom Kippur atones even for those who do not repent, but even Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi concedes that with regard to the transgressions of violating Yom Kippur itself, e.g., if one ate or performed labor on Yom Kippur, that Yom Kippur does not atone for those transgressions.

notes.he: ברייתא דקתני יוה"כ מ"מ רבי היא:
notes.en: The baraita that teaches “Yom Kippur [atones] in any case” is Rabbi.

notes.he: דהא דקתני לא התענה בו מכפר אעבירות דכל השנה אבל ההיא עבירה דעינוי לא מכפר ואך חלק נמי דקתני לעיל בעבירות דיומיה קאמר:
notes.en: Rabbi concedes with regard to the transgressions of Yom Kippur: for that which it teaches, “if he did not fast on it,” [means that it] atones for the transgressions of the whole year; but for that transgression of [not] afflicting himself it does not atone. And the “yet,” dividing, that it taught above also speaks of the transgressions of that day itself.

notes.he: ולה"ק בברייתא קמייתא דלא מכפרי והא דיליף עבירות דיומיה מחטאת ואשם דלא מכפרי ולא יליף מיה"כ גופיה דמכפר בלא תשובה אשאר עבירות משום דיליף עבירות דיומיה שיה"כ נקבע עליהם מחטאת ואשם שקבועין על אותו חטא דהכי מסתבר טפי למילף ועי"ל דה"נ קאמר תאמר ביה"כ כו' ואדילפת מחטאת ואשם תיליף ליה מיה"כ גופיה:
notes.en: And Rabbi concedes with regard to a transgression of the day itself: and this is what the first baraita says, that they do not atone. And the reason it derives the transgressions of the day itself from a sin offering and a guilt offering, which do not atone [without repentance], and does not derive [them] from Yom Kippur itself, which atones without repentance for other transgressions, is that it derives the transgressions of the day, for which Yom Kippur is fixed, from a sin offering and a guilt offering, which are fixed for that very sin, for that is the more reasonable derivation. And one can further say that this is also what it says: “Shall you say with regard to Yom Kippur,” etc., [that is,] instead of deriving it from a sin offering and a guilt offering, derive it from Yom Kippur itself.

notes.he: והיינו דקתני אך חלק:
notes.en: And Rabbi concedes with regard to the transgressions of Yom Kippur itself: and that is [why] it teaches “yet,” dividing.

messages.text: He must necessarily concede this point, as if you do not say so, then according to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, with regard to the punishment of karet for transgressing the prohibitions of Yom Kippur, since each and every hour of the day atones for one’s sins, how can you find the application of karet in this case?

notes.he: יום הכפורים אינו מכפר אלא היום כדכתיב (ויקרא ט״ז:ל׳) כי ביום הזה:
notes.en: Yom Kippur atones only [during] the day, as it is written (Leviticus 16:30): “For on this day.”

notes.he: הולך ערירי בלא בנים ואם יש לו מתים:
notes.en: Karet: he goes childless, without children; and if he has [children], they die.

notes.he: דעבירות דגופיה לא מכפר כרת לר' בעבירה דיוה"כ גופיה היכי משכחת לה:
notes.en: For if you do not say so: that it does not atone for the transgressions of the day itself, then karet, according to Rabbi, for a transgression of Yom Kippur itself, how can you find it?

messages.text: The Gemara questions this proof: And what is the difficulty? Perhaps you find a case where he performed labor the entire night of Yom Kippur and died at dawn, as in such a case there was no daytime of Yom Kippur, which is the part of Yom Kippur that effects atonement, to atone for him.
messages.quote: how can you find the application of karet in this case

notes.he: משום הא לא איריא דדילמא כי האי גוונא משכחת כרת ביוה"כ דעביד עבידתא כוליה ליליא כו':
notes.en: And what is the difficulty? On account of this there is no problem, for perhaps one finds karet on Yom Kippur in such a case: where he performed labor the whole night, etc.

messages.text: The Gemara asks: That works out well with regard to the punishment of karet for transgressing at night; but with regard to karet for transgressing at daytime, how can you find these circumstances, i.e., how can he be liable to receive karet for transgressing in the day?

notes.he: משכחת לה כדאמרת:
notes.en: That works out well for karet at night: you find it as you said.

messages.text: The Gemara responds: And what is the difficulty? Perhaps while eating bread he choked on a chunk of meat he ate with it, and died, as there was not enough time in the day after his transgression to atone for him.

notes.he: מכאן דקדק ריב"א דכרת אין זרעו נכרתים דהא הכא זרעו לא נחנקו ואתא יה"כ ומכפר עלייהו ואכתי לא משכחת לה כרת בבניו ואמר רבי כיון דבעוד הבשר בין שיניו חרה בו אף ה' ונפרע ממנו קודם שמצא שהות למצוא כפרה לא נמחל העון ונכרתין גם זרעו דליכא למימר להם נמחל שהרי הם לא חטאו:
notes.en: He choked on meat: From here the Riva inferred that with karet one’s offspring are not cut off, since here his offspring did not choke, and Yom Kippur comes and atones for them, and still you do not find karet with regard to his children. And [our] teacher said: Since, while the meat was still between his teeth, the anger of the Lord was kindled against him and He punished him before he found time to obtain atonement, the sin was not forgiven, and his offspring are also cut off; for one cannot say that it was forgiven for them, since they did not sin.

messages.text: Alternatively, it is referring to a case where he performed labor close to sunset; alternatively, it is referring to a case where as he was performing labor, the hoe with which he was working cut his thigh and he died, as in these cases too there was no time in the day after his transgression to atone for him, either because it was no longer Yom Kippur or because he died immediately.

notes.dh: אי נמי דעביד עבידתא סמוך לשקיעת החמה
notes.he: דלא הוה שהות לכפורי:
notes.en: Alternatively, where he performed labor close to sunset: so that there was no time to atone.

notes.dh: א"נ בהדי דעביד עבידתא פסקיה מרא דרפיק בה לשקיה ומית
notes.he: מיד דלא הוה שהות לכפורי:
notes.en: Alternatively, as he was performing labor, the hoe with which he was digging cut his thigh and he died: immediately, so that there was no time to atone.

notes.he: כרת משום יממא מאי קושיא דילמא כו' אלא מחוורתא כדאמר מעיקרא הא ר' אליבא דר' יהודה הא ר' אליבא דידיה:
notes.en: Karet for daytime: what is the difficulty? Perhaps, etc. Rather, it is clear as was said at first: this is Rabbi according to Rabbi Yehuda, and that is Rabbi according to his own view.

messages.caption: Two unattributed baraitot in the Sifra on whom Yom Kippur atones for, and how Abaye and Rava reconcile them.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: And the Rabbis say: The halakha is the same, i.e., there is no obligation to bring a sin offering, even with regard to the one who blasphemes, as it is stated with regard to the sin offering: “You shall have one law for him who performs the action unwittingly” (Numbers 15:29), excluding one who blasphemes, as he does not perform an action but sins with speech.

verse.he: הָאֶזְרָח בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר בְּתוֹכָם תּוֹרָה אַחַת יִהְיֶה לָכֶם לָעֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁגָגָה׃
verse.en: For the citizen among the Israelites and for the stranger who resides among them—you shall have one ritual for anyone who acts in error.

notes.he: אין מביאין על שגגתו חטאת:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: Even the blasphemer: one does not bring a sin offering for his unwitting [transgression].

messages.text: The Gemara asks: What caused the Rabbis to specify: Even one who blasphemes, as he does not perform an action? Why do the Rabbis mention this explanation?

notes.he: ה"ג מאי אף המגדף:
notes.en: This is the reading: “What is ‘even the blasphemer’?” [Rashi’s text lacks the words “as he does not perform an action”.]

notes.he: אמאי קתני (יצא) [אף] המגדף שאין בו מעשה מאי קא איירי לעיל דקאמר אף המגדף:
notes.en: Why does it teach “even the blasphemer, which involves no action”? What was being discussed above, that it says “even the blasphemer”? [The printed text is corrected here to read “even”.]

messages.text: The Gemara explains: The Rabbis heard that Rabbi Akiva teaches in his list of those who must bring a sin offering a necromancer, and he does not teach a sorcerer in his list,

notes.he: דמתני' ר"ע היא כדמפרש לקמן מגדף מביא קרבן דברי ר' עקיבא ואמרי אף מגדף נמי כידעוני. תימה לי ולר' יוחנן דאמר לעיל (כריתות דף ג:) הואיל ושניהם בלאו אחד נאמרו מאי אף דקתני במתניתין:
notes.en: They heard Rabbi Akiva: for the mishna is Rabbi Akiva’s, as is explained below: “The blasphemer brings an offering; this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.” And they said: Even the blasphemer, too, is like the sorcerer [yidde’oni]. It is puzzling to me: according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said above (3b), “since both of them are stated in a single prohibition,” what is the “even” that is taught in the mishna?

notes.dh: רבנן שמעוה לר' עקיבא דתנא בעל אוב ולא תנא ידעוני כו'
notes.he: ואומר חטאו ישא מפרש לקמן אמאי נקטו:
notes.en: The Rabbis heard Rabbi Akiva, who taught the necromancer and did not teach the sorcerer, etc. And “and it states: shall bear his sin”: it is explained below why they cited it.

messages.text: @Rabbi Akiva What is different about a sorcerer that he does not bring an offering? It must be due to the fact that his transgression does not involve an action. If so, with regard to the sin of one who blasphemes as well, it does not involve an action.

notes.he: היינו לר"ל דלעיל אבל לר"י ה"ק ליה רבנן כי היכי דפסח ומילה לא אתי קרבן דשב ואל תעשה נינהו ה"נ מגדף:
notes.en: As it does not involve an action: this is according to Reish Lakish above. But according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, this is what the Rabbis are saying to him: Just as for the Paschal offering and circumcision no offering is brought, since they are [cases of] “sit and do not act,” so too the blasphemer.

messages.text: One who unwittingly blasphemes brings an offering, since karet is stated with regard to it. This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva. And the verse states: “Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin” (Leviticus 24:15), as the Gemara will explain.

verse.he: וְאֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל תְּדַבֵּר לֵאמֹר אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי־יְקַלֵּל אֱלֹהָיו וְנָשָׂא חֶטְאוֹ׃
verse.en: And to the Israelite people speak thus: Anyone who blasphemes God shall bear the guilt;

notes.he: מפרש לקמן דכרת דמגדף איירי בקרבן עבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: And it states: “Shall bear his sin”: it is explained below that the karet of the blasphemer is speaking of the offering for idol worship.

messages.text: The Gemara asks: And is it an established principle that wherever it is written karet with regard to a mitzva, one who violates it unwittingly brings an offering? But there is the case of the mitzva of the Paschal offering, and the mitzva of circumcision, as the punishment of karet is written for failing to perform them, and yet one does not bring an offering for failing to perform these mitzvot unwittingly.
messages.quote: since karet is stated with regard to it

messages.text: 7b

The Gemara answers that this is what Rabbi Akiva is saying: One who unwittingly blasphemes brings an offering, since its punishment of karet comes, i.e., is written, in a place where the Torah discusses an offering, i.e., karet is mentioned in a passage that discusses a sin offering (see Numbers 15:27–31). This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva,

notes.he: בפרשת כי תשגו דמיירי בה בקרבנות:
notes.en: [A printer’s marker here reads: “Up to here belongs to 7a.”] Karet in the place of an offering: in the passage “And if you err” [Numbers 15:22], which speaks of offerings.

messages.text: as he maintains: Since the verse should have written karet in general, i.e., without connecting it to bringing an offering, and yet this karet is written in a place where the Torah discusses an offering, conclude from it that the unwitting blasphemer brings an offering for his transgression.

notes.he: (רבנן קאמרי ליה הגירסא הכתובה בספרים אינה כפי שיטת הש"ס וכך היא בעיני) והכי קאמרי ליה רבנן לר"ע אמרת מגדף מביא קרבן הואיל ונאמר בו כרת במקום קרבן מי סברת מגדף דקרא היינו מברך את השם מגדף היינו עובד ע"ז והאי דקתני במתני' וחכ"א אף המגדף כו' הכי קאמרי אף המגדף דידך אף מברך את השם שאתה קורא אותו מגדף:
notes.en: We arrive at the Rabbis: [A parenthetical gloss in the printed Rashi reads: “The Rabbis are saying to him; the reading written in the books does not fit the course of the Talmud, and so it appears to me.”] And this is what the Rabbis are saying to Rabbi Akiva: You said that the blasphemer brings an offering, since karet is stated with regard to him in the place of an offering. Do you think that the blasphemer [megaddef] of the verse is one who blesses [i.e., curses] the Name? The blasphemer is one who worships idols. And that which is taught in the mishna, “And the Rabbis say: Even the blasphemer,” etc., this is what they are saying: even your blasphemer, even one who blesses the Name, whom you call a blasphemer [brings no offering].

notes.he: ותימה תיפוק ליה דמביא מידי דהוי אשאר כריתות שבתורה דהא ר"ע לא בעי מעשה וכ"ש לר"ל דמעשה זוטא אית ליה ואו"ר ר' יוחנן מתרץ לטעמיה דמהכא יליף ליה ר"ע בכל התורה דלא בעינן מעשה כמו מגדף דמחייב. ור"ל מתרץ לטעמיה דמהכא יליף דסגי במעשה זוטא:
notes.en: Since karet is stated in the place of an offering: It is puzzling: let him derive that he brings [an offering] just as for the other karet transgressions in the Torah, since Rabbi Akiva does not require an action, and all the more so according to Reish Lakish, who holds that a minor action [suffices]. And [our] teacher says: Rabbi Yoḥanan answers according to his own reasoning, that from here Rabbi Akiva derives for the whole Torah that we do not require an action, as with the blasphemer, who is liable. And Reish Lakish answers according to his reasoning, that from here he derives that a minor action suffices.

messages.text: Rashi reads the next exchange differently: in his text it is the Rabbis who answer Rabbi Akiva, saying that the blasphemer of the verse is one who worships idols.

The Gemara analyzes the next clause of the baraita: And the verse states: “Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin” (Leviticus 24:15). The Gemara explains: Here we arrive at the opinion of the Rabbis, and this is what Rabbi Akiva is saying to the Rabbis:
messages.quote: And the verse states: Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin

notes.en: [This Rashi entry is empty in the source.]

notes.he: כלומר השיב ר"ע לרבנן כדמפרש ואזיל דלכרת גרידא לא איצטריך דבג"ש אתיא מפסח:
notes.en: Here we arrive at the Rabbis: that is, Rabbi Akiva answered the Rabbis, as it goes on to explain, that [the verse] would not be needed for karet alone, since that is derived by verbal analogy from the Paschal offering.

notes.he: דכתיב גבי פסח דכתיב כרת והאיש אשר הוא טהור ובדרך לא היה וגו' אתאן לרבנן דלרבנן פסח שני יליף חטאו חטאו ממברך את השם לכרת כדאמר לקמן:
notes.en: And it states: “Shall bear his sin”: which is written regarding the Paschal offering, for which karet is written: “But the man who is pure and was not on a journey,” etc. [Numbers 9:13]. Here we arrive at the Rabbis: for according to the Rabbis, the second Pesaḥ is derived [through] “his sin” and “his sin” from one who blesses the Name, for karet, as is said below.

messages.text: You say that the transgression of one who blasphemes does not involve an action, as what is the case of one who blasphemes? It is one who blesses, i.e., curses, the Name, i.e., God. But if so, then concerning the punishment of karet that is written: “That person blasphemes the Lord; and that soul shall be cut off [venikhreta] from among his people” (Numbers 15:30), for what purpose does it come, if not to render him liable to bring an offering?

verse.he: וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־תַּעֲשֶׂה ׀ בְּיָד רָמָה מִן־הָאֶזְרָח וּמִן־הַגֵּר אֶת־יְהֹוָה הוּא מְגַדֵּף וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מִקֶּרֶב עַמָּהּ׃
verse.en: But whether citizen or stranger, the person who acts defiantly reviles GOD; that person shall be cut off from among their people.

notes.dh: אלא כרת במברך את השם מנא להו
notes.he: במברך את השם כתיב איש כי יקלל אלהיו ונשא חטאו (ויקרא כ״ד:ט״ו) ונאמר בפסח (במדבר ט׳:י״ג) חטאו ישא האיש ההוא מה להלן כרת אף כאן כרת והכי נמי איכא דדריש ליה בפסחים בפרק מי שהיה טמא (פסחים דף צג:) ודרשי הכי וחדל לעשות הפסח ראשון דהא קרבן ה' לא הקריב במועדו חטאו ישא ולא נאמר כרת דמגדף במקום קרבן ולא גמרינן ליה אלא מכרת דפסח שאינה בת חטאת דמצות עשה היא. ור"ע אית ליה כרת בשני ומוקי לחטאו ישא בפסח שני וגמר לה ממגדף וסבר מגדף היינו מברך את השם ובפסחים (שם) נמי איכא דדריש ליה הכי:
notes.en: But karet for one who blesses the Name, from where do they [derive it]? With regard to one who blesses the Name it is written: “Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin” (Leviticus 24:15), and it is stated with regard to the Paschal offering (Numbers 9:13): “That man shall bear his sin.” Just as there it is karet, so too here it is karet. And so too there is one who expounds it this way in Pesaḥim, in the chapter Mi SheHaya Tamei (Pesaḥim 93b), and they expound thus: “And refrains from performing the Pesaḥ” is the first [Pesaḥ]; “because he did not bring the offering of the Lord in its appointed time, he shall bear his sin” [is also the first]. And [so] the karet of the blasphemer was not stated in the place of an offering, and we derive it only from the karet of the Paschal offering, which is not subject to a sin offering, since it is a positive mitzva. And Rabbi Akiva holds that there is karet for the second [Pesaḥ], and he applies “shall bear his sin” to the second Pesaḥ and derives it from the blasphemer, and he holds that the blasphemer is one who blesses the Name. And in Pesaḥim (ibid.) too there is one who expounds it this way.

notes.he: והכין אמר להון ר' עקיבא לרבנן אמריתו מגדף (ליה) [לית] ביה מעשה ולא אתא כרת דיהא לקרבן מיהו מודיתו לי דמגדף היינו מברך את השם ומשום הכי לית ביה קרבן דסבריתו (דעקיצת) [דעקימת] שפתיו לא הוי מעשה כלל ולדידי אפי' הכי חייב קרבן ואלא לדידכו אמאי כתיב כרת במגדף:
notes.en: And thus Rabbi Akiva said to them, to the Rabbis: You said that the blasphemer involves no action and the karet did not come [to teach] that there is an offering. However, you concede to me that the blasphemer is one who blesses the Name, and that for this reason there is no offering for it, since you hold that the twisting of his lips is no action at all; while according to me, even so he is liable to an offering. But according to you, why is karet written regarding the blasphemer?

messages.text: It comes to give the punishment of karet to one who curses God, in order to teach that the phrase: “Shall bear his sin,” written in the verse: “Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin” (Leviticus 24:15), is referring to karet, so that one can derive by verbal analogy that an individual who was obligated to bring a Paschal offering for the second Pesaḥ and did not do so is likewise liable to receive karet.
messages.quote: for what purpose does it come

notes.he: אמרין ליתו כרת למברך את השם דהיינו מגדף ולמילף מינה כרת לפסח שני דהא כתיב הכא במברך ונשא חטאו ואית ביה כרת וכתיב בפסח שני חטאו ישא מה להלן כרת במברך אף כאן בפסח שני בכרת ואע"ג דכתיב גבי פסח כרת דכתיב והאיש אשר הוא טהור ובדרך לא היה:
notes.en: They say [to him]: To give karet to one who blesses the Name, who is the blasphemer, and to derive from it karet for the second Pesaḥ. For it is written here, regarding one who blesses, “he shall bear his sin,” and there is karet for it, and it is written regarding the second Pesaḥ, “he shall bear his sin.” Just as there, with one who blesses, it is karet, so too here, with the second Pesaḥ, it is karet; even though karet is written regarding the Paschal offering, as it is written: “But the man who is pure and was not on a journey.”

messages.text: As it is written with regard to one who curses God: “Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin,” and it is written with regard to one who was obligated to bring a Paschal offering for the second Pesaḥ and did not do so: “That man shall bear his sin” (Numbers 9:13). Just as there, with regard to one who curses God it is referring to the punishment of karet, so too here, with regard to the Paschal offering it is referring to the punishment of karet.

verse.he: וְהָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־הוּא טָהוֹר וּבְדֶרֶךְ לֹא־הָיָה וְחָדַל לַעֲשׂוֹת הַפֶּסַח וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מֵעַמֶּיהָ כִּי ׀ קׇרְבַּן יְהֹוָה לֹא הִקְרִיב בְּמֹעֲדוֹ חֶטְאוֹ יִשָּׂא הָאִישׁ הַהוּא׃
verse.en: But if anyone who is pure and not on a journey refrains from offering the passover sacrifice, that person shall be cut off from kin, for GOD’s offering was not presented at its set time; that party shall bear the guilt.

notes.he: רבנן כר' סבירא להו כפלוגתא דר' ור' נתן דאמר במסכת פסחים בפרק מי שהיה טמא חייב על הראשון וחייב על השני דברי ר' ר' נתן אומר חייב על הראשון ופטור על השני ותרוויהו ילפי מהאי קרא והאיש אשר הוא טמא ר' סבר וחדל לעשות הפסח ראשון ונכרת אי נמי כי את קרבן ה' לא הקריב במועדו בשני חטאו ישא היינו כרת דיליף מונשא חטאו דמברך דהיינו מגדף ור' נתן סבר וחדל לעשות הפסח ונכרתה דהא קרבן ה' לא הקריב במועדו בראשון והאי חטאו ישא מאי עביד ליה קסבר מגדף לאו היינו מברך את השם אלא מזמר לפני ע"ז וגמר ונשא חטאו דמברך מחטאו ישא דפסח מה חטאו דפסח כרת אף חטאו דמברך כרת ור' עקיבא גמר כרת למברך מחטאו דפסח כר' נתן אייתר ליה כרת דמגדף לקרבן. לישנא אחרינא בשלמא לדידי להכי כתב כרת במגדף במקום קרבן לחייבו קרבן אע"ג דאין בו מעשה ומגדף דהיינו מומר לעבודת כוכבים אלא לדידכו דאמריתו מגדף לית ביה מעשה ופטור מקרבן אמאי כתב כרת במגדף אמרו ליה ליתן כרת למברך את השם אמר להן א"כ לדידכו לית (להו) [לכו] מגדף היינו מומר ומהו מגדף עצמו אמרו היינו מברך את השם וילפינן מיניה נמי כרת לפסח שני כדאמר לעיל ור' עקיבא יליף כרת למברך מפסח כר' נתן:
notes.en:
The Rabbis hold like Rabbi, according to the dispute between Rabbi and Rabbi Natan stated in tractate Pesaḥim, in the chapter Mi SheHaya Tamei: [One is] liable for the first and liable for the second; this is the statement of Rabbi. Rabbi Natan says: Liable for the first and exempt for the second. And both derive it from this verse: “But the man who is pure” [Numbers 9:13]. Rabbi holds: “and refrains from performing the Pesaḥ” refers to the first, “and [that soul] shall be cut off”; alternatively, “because he did not bring the offering of the Lord in its appointed time” refers to the second, “he shall bear his sin,” which is karet, derived from “and shall bear his sin” of one who blesses [the Name], who is the blasphemer. And Rabbi Natan holds: “and refrains from performing the Pesaḥ, that soul shall be cut off,” for “he did not bring the offering of the Lord in its appointed time” refers to the first. And what does he do with this “shall bear his sin”? He holds that the blasphemer is not one who blesses the Name but one who sings before idols, and he derives “and shall bear his sin” of one who blesses from “shall bear his sin” of the Paschal offering: just as “his sin” of the Paschal offering is karet, so too “his sin” of one who blesses is karet. And Rabbi Akiva derives karet for one who blesses from “his sin” of the Paschal offering, like Rabbi Natan; [so] the karet of the blasphemer is left over for [teaching] an offering.
Another version: Granted, according to me, for this reason karet is written regarding the blasphemer in the place of an offering: to make him liable to an offering even though it involves no action, and the blasphemer is an apostate for idol worship. But according to you, who say that the blasphemer involves no action and is exempt from an offering, why is karet written regarding the blasphemer? They said to him: To give karet to one who blesses the Name. He said to them: If so, according to you, the blasphemer is not the apostate; then what is the blasphemer itself? They said: It is one who blesses the Name, and we derive from it also karet for the second Pesaḥ, as was said above. And Rabbi Akiva derives karet for one who blesses from the Paschal offering, like Rabbi Natan.

messages.text: This is like a person who says to another: You cleaned [geirafta] the bowl and rendered it lacking, i.e., the transgression of blasphemy is so severe that it is compared to one who does actual damage to God.
messages.lead: With regard to one who blasphemes, the Sages taught in a baraita: The verse states: “That person blasphemes [megaddef] the Lord” (Numbers 15:30).

notes.he: ר' מתחלפת בד'. הנחת את הקערה מן התבשיל וחסרת גם את העץ. קסבר מגדף היינו מברך את השם ומילתא רבה עבד דפשט ידו בעיקר:
notes.en: Geirafta: the resh is interchangeable with the dalet [so giddef, “blaspheme,” is like geiref, “scrape clean”]. You emptied the bowl of the cooked food and you also diminished the wood [of the bowl]. He holds that the blasphemer is one who blesses [i.e., curses] the Name, and he has done a grave thing, for he stretched out his hand against the Fundamental [i.e., God].

messages.text: Isi ben Yehuda maintains that the case of the blasphemer is identical to that of one who blesses, i.e., curses, the Name, i.e., God, which is a particularly severe transgression.

This is like a person who says to another: You cleaned the bowl and removed its contents, but did not render it lacking, i.e., the transgression of blasphemy is not compared to one who does actual damage to God.

notes.dh: ולא חסרת קסבר היינו עובד עבודת כוכבים
notes.he: כגון משורר ומזמר לעבודת כוכבים דלאו מילתא רבה היא כולי האי:
notes.en: And did not diminish: he holds that this is one who worships idols, for example, one who sings and plays music for idol worship, which is not so grave a matter.

notes.he: פי' שלא כילה לגמרי. לא חיסרת. פי' לא חיסרת דבר אלא כילה לגמרי כלומר פשט ידו בעיקר שעבד עבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: You cleaned it and diminished it: that is, he did not finish it entirely. Did not diminish it: that is, you did not leave anything lacking but finished it entirely; that is to say, he stretched out his hand against the Fundamental, in that he worshipped idols.

messages.text: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya maintains that the case of the blasphemer is the same as that of an idol worshipper, which is a less severe transgression.

notes.he: פירש"י מזמר ומשורר לעבודת כוכבים וקשה אמאי פירש כן אי משום דלית ביה מעשה לימא כגון שקיבלו באלוה שאמר לו אלי אתה אלא נראה דמגדף היינו עובד עבודת כוכבים בזיבוח וקיטור והיינו כרת דכתיב בעבודת כוכבים ולא פליגי אלא במברך את השם:
notes.en: The blasphemer is one who worships idols: Rashi explained: one who sings and plays music for idol worship. And it is difficult: why did he explain it so? If because it involves no action, let him say, for example, that he accepted it as a god, saying to it: You are my god. Rather, it appears that the blasphemer is one who worships idols by slaughtering and burning incense, and that is the karet written with regard to idol worship; and they disagree only about one who blesses the Name.

notes.he: מגדף קא מפרש כגון גורף קערה וחיסר מן הקערה עצמה קסבר מגדף היינו מברך את השם כלומר שפושט יד וכופר בעיקר. גורף קערה ולא חיסרה קסבר מגדף היינו עובד עבודת כוכבים משורר לע"ז גירף קערה שכפר בעיקר ולא חיסרה שלא פשט ידו בשם הקדש:
notes.en: The blasphemer is explained: like one who scrapes a bowl and diminishes the bowl itself: he holds that the blasphemer is one who blesses the Name, that is to say, who stretches out his hand and denies the Fundamental. One who scrapes the bowl and does not diminish it: he holds that the blasphemer is one who worships idols, who sings for idolatry: he scraped the bowl, in that he denied the Fundamental, but did not diminish it, in that he did not stretch out his hand against the holy Name.

messages.text: The verse is speaking of an idol worshipper.
messages.lead: This dispute as to the nature of the transgression of the blasphemer is taught in another baraita: “That person blasphemes the Lord” (Numbers 15:30), and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

messages.text: The verse comes only to give the punishment of karet to one who blesses, i.e., curses, the Name, i.e., God.
Mishna

There are some women who bring a sin offering of a woman after childbirth and the offering is eaten by the priests. And there are some women who bring a sin offering but it is not eaten. And there are some women who do not bring a sin offering at all.
The mishna elaborates: The following women bring a sin offering and it is eaten by the priests:

One who miscarries a fetus with a form similar to a domesticated animal, one who miscarries a fetus with a form similar to an undomesticated animal, or one who miscarries a fetus with a form similar to a bird; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: מפרש טעמא במסכת נדה בפרק המפלת (נדה כב:) הואיל ונאמרה בו יצירה כאדם:
notes.en: Mishna. Like a domesticated animal, an undomesticated animal or a bird: the reason is explained in tractate Nidda, in the chapter HaMappelet (Nidda 22b): since “forming” is stated with regard to it, as with a person.

notes.he: שנאמר בהן יצירה כמו באדם:
notes.en: One who miscarries [a form] like a domesticated animal, an undomesticated animal or a bird: since “forming” is stated with regard to them as with a person.

messages.text: She does not bring a sin offering unless the fetus has the form of a person.

With regard to a woman who miscarries a sandal fetus, i.e., one that has the form of a flat fish; or if she miscarries the placenta; or an amniotic sac in which tissue developed; or a fetus that emerged cut, i.e., in pieces; and likewise a Canaanite maidservant, owned by a Jew, who miscarried; in all these cases she brings a sin offering and it is eaten by the priests.

notes.he: ולד הוא אלא שנפחתה צורתו:
notes.en: A sandal: it is a fetus, but its form has been spoiled.

notes.he: נמי אמרינן במסכת נדה בהמפלת (נדה דף כו.) אין שיליא בלא ולד. ושפיר היינו עור הולד מרוקם שיש בתוך השפיר צורת איברים קטנים ובמס' נדה מפרש לה בהמפלת:
notes.en: A placenta: we also say in tractate Nidda, in the chapter HaMappelet (Nidda 26a): there is no placenta without a fetus. And an amniotic sac in which tissue developed: the skin of the fetus, developed, so that inside the sac there is the form of small limbs; it is explained in tractate Nidda, in the chapter HaMappelet.

notes.he: כנענית ובגמ' פריך למה לי למתניי':
notes.en: And likewise a maidservant: a Canaanite one; and in the Gemara it asks why [the mishna] needs to teach it.

notes.he: ולד שנתקלקלה צורתו ושפיר מרוקם כדאמר במס' נדה תחלת ברייתו מראשו ב' עיניו כב' טיפי זבוב:
notes.en: One who miscarries a sandal: a fetus whose form was spoiled. And an amniotic sac in which tissue developed: as is said in tractate Nidda: the beginning of its formation is from its head, its two eyes like two drops of a fly.

notes.he: דאין שליא בלא ולד אלא שנימוח:
notes.en: Or a placenta: for there is no placenta without a fetus, but it dissolved.

notes.he: שהוציא החיה אברים אברים:
notes.en: And one that emerged cut: which the midwife brought out limb by limb.

messages.text: And these women bring sin offerings but their sin offerings are not eaten: One who miscarries and does not know the nature of what she miscarried;

notes.he: אם צורת אדם וחייבת או דגים וחגבים ופטורה:
notes.en: And does not know what she miscarried: whether it had a human form, so that she is liable, or [was like] fish and grasshoppers, so that she is exempt.

notes.he: שתי תורים [א' לעולה וא' לחטאת ועל של] עולה מתנה עלה אם מין חובה ילדה תהא לחובתה ואם לאו תהא עולת נדבה אבל חטאת לא מצי לאתנויי דאין חטאת נדבה ומחייב בספק ואינו נאכל דשמא לאו בת קרבן היא ומליקתה כנבילה בעלמא ומשום חולין על המזבח לא איכפת לן דכיון דאין למזבח אלא דמה לא חשיבא אכילה ובמסכת נזיר (דף כט.) ילפינן דחטאת העוף באה על הספק:
notes.en: Bring an offering: two turtledoves, [one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering]. With regard to the burnt offering she stipulates: If I gave birth to a type that obligates, let it be for my obligation, and if not, let it be a voluntary burnt offering. But with regard to the sin offering she cannot stipulate, since there is no voluntary sin offering. And she is obligated [to bring it] in a case of uncertainty, and it is not eaten, since perhaps she is not subject to an offering, and its melika [killing by pinching the neck] would be like that of a mere carcass.
