And as for [bringing] non-sacred [birds] onto the altar, we are not concerned, since only its blood goes to the altar, and that is not considered eating. And in tractate Nazir (29a) we derive that a bird sin offering may come for an uncertainty.

notes.he: אם נפל הפילה או רוח הפילה:
notes.en: And does not know what she miscarried: whether she miscarried a fetus or miscarried wind.

notes.he: אינו נאכל אלא ישרף או יקבר:
notes.en: They bring: it is not eaten, but is to be burned or buried.

messages.text: and two women who miscarried, in a case where one miscarried a fetus of a type for which a woman is exempt from bringing an offering and the other one miscarried a fetus of a type for which a woman is liable to bring an offering, and they do not know which miscarried which type.

notes.he: במחבואה:
notes.en: And likewise two women who miscarried: in a hidden place.

notes.he: דגים וחגבים:
notes.en: One of a type that exempts: fish and grasshoppers.

notes.he: סנדל או שיליא ואין ידוע אי זו הפילה פטור ואי זו הפילה חובה מביאות כל אחת שתי תורים כמו שפירשתי ואינו נאכל:
notes.en: And one of a type that obligates: a sandal or a placenta, and it is not known which one miscarried the exempting type and which one the obligating type. Each one brings two turtledoves, as I explained, and it is not eaten.

notes.he: כהללו דאמר לקמיה שפיר מלא מים וכו' ואין ידוע איזו ילדה מין פטור:
notes.en: One of a type that exempts: like those it mentions afterward, an amniotic sac full of water, etc.; and it is not known which one gave birth to the exempting type.

messages.text: When is their sin offering not eaten? It is when both women went to different places within the Temple to bring their offerings, e.g., this woman went to the east and that woman went to the west. But if both of them were standing together, both of them together bring one sin offering, and it is eaten.

notes.he: אינו נאכל בזמן שהלכה כו' שאינן יכולות להתנות שהביאו קיניהן לכהן והלכו לדרכן:
notes.en: When: is it not eaten? When they went, etc., for they cannot stipulate, since they brought their nests [pairs of birds] to the priest and went on their way.

notes.he: בגמ' מפרש מאי עבדן:
notes.en: But if both of them were standing, etc.: the Gemara explains what they do.

notes.he: א"ר יוסי אימתי אינו נאכל בזמן שהלכו זו למזרח או למערב דאינן יכול להתנות אבל אם היו שתיהן עומדות כאן מביאות קרבן ונאכל דמתנו כל אחת אומרת לחברתה אם אני הפלתי מין פטור ואת מין חיוב יהא חלקי נתון לך הלכך מביאין ונאכל:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei said: When is it not eaten? When they went, this one to the east and that one to the west, so that they cannot stipulate. But if both of them were standing here, they bring an offering and it is eaten, for they stipulate: each one says to her fellow, If I miscarried the exempting type and you the obligating type, let my share be given to you. Therefore they bring it and it is eaten.

messages.text: These women do not bring a sin offering: A woman who miscarries an amniotic sac full of water, or one full of blood, or one full of different colors; and likewise a woman who miscarries a fetus with a form similar to fish, or grasshoppers, or repugnant creatures, or creeping animals;

notes.he: גוונים:
notes.en: Genunin: colors.

notes.he: (כמין דגים וחגבים):
notes.en: (Like fish and grasshoppers.) [A heading only, with no comment.]

notes.he: גוונים בלא צורה:
notes.en: Full of genunim: colors without form.

messages.text: and a woman who miscarries on the fortieth day of her pregnancy; and a woman who gives birth by caesarean section.

notes.he: במסכת נדה בפ' המפלת (נדה דף ל.) עד שיעברו מ' יום להריון הוי מיא בעלמא:
notes.en: One who miscarries on the fortieth day: in tractate Nidda, in the chapter HaMappelet (Nidda 30a): until forty days of pregnancy have passed, it is mere water.

notes.he: לעיבורה שאין הוולד נוצר אלא לסוף מ"א יום:
notes.en: One who miscarries on the fortieth day: of her pregnancy, for the fetus is formed only at the end of forty-one days.

notes.he: כגון שנגממו כותלי בית הרחם ואח"כ יצא:
notes.en: And a caesarean section: for example, where the walls of the womb were cut open and then it emerged.

messages.text: Rabbi Shimon deems a woman liable to bring a sin offering in the case where she gives birth by caesarean section.

messages.caption: The mishna’s three groups: women who bring an offering that is eaten, women who bring one that is not eaten, and women who bring none.

messages.text: Gemara
From where do we derive that in the case of a Canaanite maidservant, owned by a Jew, who miscarried, she brings a sin offering and it is eaten? As the Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: and likewise a Canaanite maidservant, owned by a Jew, who miscarried

notes.he: גמ' ושפחה מנלן דת"ר דבר אל בני ישראל אשה כי תזריע:
notes.en: Gemara. And a maidservant, from where do we [derive it]? As the Sages taught: “Speak to the children of Israel … if a woman conceives.”

messages.text: The passage discussing the halakhot of a woman following childbirth begins with the verse: “Speak to the children of Israel, saying: If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male” (Leviticus 12:2). From this verse I have derived only that the full-fledged children of Israel are included in these halakhot; from where do I derive that a convert and a Canaanite maidservant are also included in these halakhot? The verse states “a woman,” which includes other women.

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר אִשָּׁה כִּי תַזְרִיעַ וְיָלְדָה זָכָר וְטָמְאָה שִׁבְעַת יָמִים כִּימֵי נִדַּת דְּוֺתָהּ תִּטְמָא׃
verse.en: Speak to the Israelite people thus: When a woman at childbirth, lit. “brings forth seed.” bears a male, she shall be impure seven days; she shall be impure as at the time of her condition of menstrual separation.—

messages.text: The Gemara asks: What is the meaning of the special emphasis in the mishna: And likewise a Canaanite maidservant? Why does the mishna deem it necessary to write this halakha?

notes.he: הא פשיטא לן דכל מצוה שהאשה חייבת בה עבד חייב בה דגמרי לה לה כתיב באשה (דברים כ״ד:א׳) וכתב לה ספר כריתות וכתיב בשפחה או חפשה לא נתן לה:
notes.en: What is [the need for] “and likewise a maidservant”? It is obvious to us that in every mitzva in which a woman is obligated a slave is obligated, as we derive it from [the word] “to her”: it is written with regard to a woman (Deuteronomy 24:1), “and he shall write her [lah] a bill of divorce,” and it is written with regard to a maidservant, “nor was freedom given to her [lah]” [Leviticus 19:20].

notes.he: מאי וכן שפחה פשיטא דהא איתרבי:
notes.en: What is “and likewise a maidservant”? It is obvious, for she has been included [by the verse].

messages.text: The Gemara answers: It might enter your mind to say that when we say: With regard to any mitzva in which a woman is obligated a Canaanite slave is also obligated in that mitzva, this statement applies with regard to a matter that is the same for a man and for a woman.

notes.dh: הני מילי בדבר ששוה בין באיש בין באשה
notes.he: כגון עשה שלא הזמן גרמא:
notes.en: This applies to a matter that is the same for a man and a woman: such as a positive mitzva that is not time-bound.

messages.text: But with regard to the offerings of a woman after childbirth, which is a category that applies to women but does not apply to men, one might say a Canaanite maidservant is not obligated to bring these offerings. It is for this reason the mishna taught the case of a Canaanite maidservant.

notes.he: תימה אה"נ ואיצטריך קרא לגיורת דאמרי' בספרי גבי ברכת כהנים כל מקום שמדבר בישראל צריך להביא הגרים:
notes.en: Say a maidservant is not obligated: It is puzzling: [why not say that] indeed this is so, and the verse is needed for a convert woman? For we say in the Sifrei with regard to the priestly blessing: wherever it speaks of Israel, one needs [a verse] to include the converts.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: These women bring a sin offering but their sin offerings are not eaten. It then teaches that in a case where one miscarried a fetus of a type for which a woman is exempt from bringing an offering and the other one miscarried a fetus of a type for which a woman is obligated to bring an offering, Rabbi Yosei maintains that if both are standing together they bring one offering together.
messages.quote: both of them together bring one sin offering, and it is eaten

messages.text: The Gemara asks: What exactly do they do? The two of them bring one definite burnt offering, and a sin offering of a bird due to uncertainty, and they each stipulate that if she is obligated to bring the sin offering the animal is hers, and if not then it belongs to the other woman.

notes.he: לרבי יוסי מתיין תרוייהו חד קרבן בין שתיהן יקנו חטאת העוף חדא ודאי עולת העוף תביא כל אחת ודאי ובתנאי שאם אינה חייבת תהא נדבה אבל חטאת העוף לא מצי למימר תהא נדבה דאין חטאת נדבה ולהכי מייתו חטאת העוף ויקנוהו בין שתיהן ומתנין אם אני חייבת יהא חלקך מחול לי ואם את חייבת יהא חלקי מחול לך וממ"נ הויא מליקתה כשרה:
notes.en: What do they do? According to Rabbi Yosei, the two of them bring one offering between them: they acquire one bird sin offering jointly. A definite bird burnt offering each one brings definitely, on condition that if she is not obligated it shall be a voluntary offering. But of the bird sin offering she cannot say, “Let it be voluntary,” since there is no voluntary sin offering. Therefore they bring a bird sin offering, acquire it jointly and stipulate: If I am obligated, let your share be forgone to me, and if you are obligated, let my share be forgone to you. And either way, its melika is valid.

notes.he: חד קרבן קנין וודאי חד קרבן דלעולה מייתי ודאי בלא תנאי משום דעולה דורון בעלמא הוא:
notes.en: One offering, a definite one: one offering they bring definitely, for a burnt offering, without a stipulation, because a burnt offering is merely a gift.

notes.he: וחטאת העוף שנאכל לכהנים מייתו בספק ומתנין:
notes.en: And the bird sin offering, which is eaten by the priests, they bring in uncertainty and stipulate.

messages.text: The Gemara asks: And is Rabbi Yosei of the opinion that a stipulation is effective in the case of a sin offering? But didn’t we learn in a mishna (23a):

notes.dh: ומי אית ליה לר' יוסי תנאיה
notes.he: והא תנן בהא מסכת בפרק דם שחיטה בחתיכה של חלב וחתיכה של חולין ר' שמעון אומר שניהן מביאין חטאת כו':
notes.en: And is Rabbi Yosei of the opinion that a stipulation [is effective]? But we learned in this tractate, in the chapter Dam Sheḥita, regarding a piece of forbidden fat and a piece of non-sacred [fat]: Rabbi Shimon says: The two of them bring a sin offering, etc.

messages.text: They both bring one sin offering together,
messages.lead: With regard to a situation where one of two women unwittingly ate a piece of forbidden fat and is obligated to bring a sin offering, but it is unknown which woman,

notes.he: בפרק דם שחיטה לקמן (כריתות דף כג.):
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says, etc.: in the chapter Dam Sheḥita below (Keritot 23a).

notes.he: תימה דהא בעי סמיכה ושניהן א"א לסמוך דאחד מהן יעשה עבודה בקדשים:
notes.en: Both bring one sin offering: It is puzzling, since it requires leaning [semikha], and both cannot lean on it, for one of them would be performing labor with a consecrated animal.

messages.text: They do not both bring one sin offering together.
Evidently, Rabbi Yosei is not of the opinion that a stipulation is effective with regard to a sin offering.

Rabbi Yosei concedes that a stipulation is effective with regard to one who has not yet brought an atonement offering to complete the purification process, as is the case concerning a woman after childbirth.

notes.he: דמתני' בארבעה מחוסרי כפרה דלא מייתי קרבן לשום חטאת אלא לאשתרויי בקדשים:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei concedes: [with regard to] our mishna, in the chapter Arba’a Meḥusarei Kappara, where they do not bring the offering as a sin offering [for a sin] but to become permitted to eat consecrated food.

notes.he: כגון מתניתי' דיולדת דהיינו מחוסר כפרה דמתיין ומתנין:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei concedes with regard to one who lacks atonement: as in our mishna about a woman after childbirth, who is one who lacks atonement, that they bring and stipulate.

messages.text: Rabbi Yosei concedes with regard to one who has not yet brought an atonement offering that a stipulation is effective.
messages.lead: And likewise, when Ravin came from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

messages.text: The Gemara asks: What is the reason for this difference between the sin offering of one who has not yet brought an atonement offering and standard sin offerings? The Gemara answers: There, with regard to a sin offering brought for a transgression, the man requires definite awareness of his transgression for him to be obligated to bring a sin offering, as it is written: “If his sin, which he has sinned, be known to him” (Leviticus 4:28).

verse.he: אוֹ הוֹדַע אֵלָיו חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא וְהֵבִיא קׇרְבָּנוֹ שְׂעִירַת עִזִּים תְּמִימָה נְקֵבָה עַל־חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא׃
verse.en: or the sin of which they are guilty is made known—that person shall bring a female goat without blemish as an offering for the aforementioned sin.

notes.he: גבי חטאת חלב בפרק דם שחיטה גברא בעי ידיעה שידע שחטא ואי לא מייתי כל חד אשם תלוי ולא חטאת בשותפות:
notes.en: There: regarding a sin offering for forbidden fat, in the chapter Dam Sheḥita, the man requires awareness, that he know that he sinned; and if not, each one brings a provisional guilt offering, and not a sin offering in partnership.

notes.he: בחתיכה של חלב וחתיכה שומן של חולין מ"ט דר' יוסי דאין מביאין חטאת אחת דהתם בעי ידיעה כו':
notes.en: What is the reason there? With a piece of forbidden fat and a piece of non-sacred fat, what is Rabbi Yosei’s reason that they do not bring one sin offering? For there awareness is required, etc.

messages.text: Therefore, in the case where one of two women ate forbidden fat, they do not bring a sin offering together and stipulate that it should be for whichever of them ate the forbidden fat. But here, with regard to a woman after a miscarriage, when these women bring their sin offering they do so only in order to become permitted in the consumption of sacrificial food, and therefore the stipulation is effective.
With regard to any sin offering that comes as atonement for a sin, two people do not bring it together.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites a proof that this distinction is in fact the opinion of Rabbi Yosei: As it is taught in the latter clause of that mishna that

notes.he: בפ' דם שחיטה (שם) כל חטאת שהיא באה על חטא אלמא באה על חטא דוקא נקט:
notes.en: As it teaches in the latter clause of that one: in the chapter Dam Sheḥita (ibid.): “Any sin offering that comes for a sin.” Evidently it specifies precisely “that comes for a sin.”

notes.he: כדקתני סיפא בההיא מתני' דדם שחיטה ר' יוסי אומר כל חטאת כו':
notes.en: As it teaches in the latter clause of that mishna, in Dam Sheḥita: Rabbi Yosei says: Any sin offering, etc.

messages.text: This indicates that if a sin offering does not atone for a sin, two people can bring it together.

§ The mishna teaches: And these women do not bring a sin offering, and among them are a woman who gives birth by caesarean section. Rabbi Shimon deems a woman liable to bring an offering in a case where she gives birth by caesarean section. The Gemara asks: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
messages.quote: Rabbi Shimon deems a woman liable to bring a sin offering in the case where she gives birth by caesarean section

notes.he: פי' ע"י סם פתחו לכריסה והוציאו הולד. ור"י לוי פי' דיצא דרך בית הרעי ואין נראה מדקאמר בפ"ק דבכורות גבי דג טמא שבלע דג טהור כגון שנמצא דרך בית הרעי ש"מ שא"א לצאת דרך בית הרעי אא"כ בלע שנכנס דרך הוושט אבל מה שמשריץ בתוך מיעיו לא יצא דרך בית הרעי:
notes.en: Caesarean section [yotzei dofen]: that is, by means of a drug they opened her abdomen and took out the fetus. And Rabbi Y. Levi explained that it came out by way of the rectum. And this does not appear correct, from what is said in the first chapter of Bekhorot regarding a non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish, for example, where it was found in the rectum: conclude from it that it is impossible [for something] to exit by way of the rectum unless it was swallowed and entered through the esophagus, but what is spawned within the innards does not exit by way of the rectum.

messages.text: The verse states: “But if she bears a girl” (Leviticus 12:5). The term “she bears” is superfluous in the context of the passage, and it serves to include another type of birth, and what is it? This is a birth by caesarean section.

verse.he: וְאִם־נְקֵבָה תֵלֵד וְטָמְאָה שְׁבֻעַיִם כְּנִדָּתָהּ וְשִׁשִּׁים יוֹם וְשֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֵּשֵׁב עַל־דְּמֵי טׇהֳרָהֿ׃
verse.en: If she bears a female, she shall be impure two weeks as during her menstruation, and she shall remain in a state of blood purification for sixty-six days.

notes.he: הוה ליה למכתב ואם נקבה היא:
notes.en: “But if she bears a girl”: it should have written: “But if it is a girl.”

notes.he: דהוי מיעוט אחר מיעוט דוילדה ותלד משמע ולא יוצא דופן:
notes.en: “She bears,” to include: for it is a restriction after a restriction, for “and gives birth” and “she bears” [each] imply: and not a caesarean section.

notes.he: תלד יתירא הוא לרבות לידה אחרת:
notes.en: “She bears” is superfluous, to include another birth.

messages.text: The Gemara asks: And as for the Rabbis, what is their reasoning?

Their ruling is derived from the verse: “If a woman conceives [tazria] and gives birth to a male” (Leviticus 12:2). The word tazria literally means to receive seed, indicating that all the halakhot mentioned in that passage do not apply unless she gives birth through the place where she receives seed, not through any other place, such as in the case of a caesarean section.

notes.he: דרך רחם ממש:
notes.en: From the place where she receives seed: through the womb itself.

messages.text: Mishna

A woman who gives birth to a daughter counts fourteen days during which she is ritually impure. That is followed by sixty-six days during which she remains ritually pure even if she experiences a flow of blood. The Torah obligates a woman to bring her offering on the eighty-first day (see Leviticus 12:1–6). If the woman miscarries another fetus before that day, she is not required to bring an additional offering.

In the case of a woman who miscarries a fetus on the night of, i.e., preceding, the eighty-first day, Beit Shammai deem her exempt from bringing a second offering and Beit Hillel deem her liable to bring a second offering.

notes.he: שילדה נקבה לאור פ"א שהיתה ראויה למחר להביא כפרתה הפילה:
notes.en: Mishna. On the night of the eighty-first: one who had given birth to a girl miscarried on the night of the eighty-first, when she was fit to bring her atonement offering the next day.

notes.he: מלידה ב' אע"ג דלאחר מלאת הוא הואיל ולילה הוא ולא יצאה שעה ראויה לקרבן דלילה מחוסר זמן קרבן הוא דכתיב (ויקרא ז׳:ל״ח) ביום צותו הילכך לענין קרבן כתוך מלאת דמי:
notes.en: Beit Shammai exempt her from the offering: for the second birth. Even though it is after the completion [of her days], since it is night, she did not emerge into a time fit for an offering, for the night is lacking the time for an offering, as it is written (Leviticus 7:38): “On the day that He commanded.” Therefore, with regard to the offering, it is as though it were within the completion [of her days].

notes.he: בימי טהרה דיולדת נקבה מיירי:
notes.en: On the night of the eighty-first: it speaks of the days of purity of a woman who gave birth to a girl.

notes.he: בית שמאי פוטרין אותה מקרבן שני דקסברי הואיל ולא הפילה בשעה שראויה להביא קרבן על הלידה הראשונה נפטרת בקרבן ראשון:
notes.en: Beit Shammai exempt her from a second offering, for they hold: since she did not miscarry at a time fit for bringing the offering for the first birth, she is exempted by the first offering.

messages.text: What is different between the night of the eighty-first and the day of the eighty-first? If they are equal with regard to the halakhot of ritual impurity, i.e., the blood flow of this woman on the eighty-first night renders her ritually impure and all the standard strictures of ritual impurity apply to her, will the two time periods not be equal with regard to liability to bring an additional offering as well?

notes.he: דודאי חייבת כדמפרש לקמן בפ' ארבעה מחוסרי כפרה (כריתות דף ט.):
notes.en: What is different between the night of the eighty-first and the day of the eighty-first: for [if she miscarries on the day] she is certainly obligated, as is explained below in the chapter Arba’a Meḥusarei Kappara (Keritot 9a).

notes.he: שהרי אתם מודים שמשקיעת החמה של יום פ' כלו ימי טוהר שלה ואם ראתה בליל פ"א טמאה:
notes.en: If they are equal with regard to impurity: for you concede that from sunset of the eightieth day her days of purity have ended, and if she saw [blood] on the night of the eighty-first she is impure.

notes.he: כדמפרשי טעמא אם שוה לו ליל פ"א ליום פ"א לטומאה דלדברי הכל צריכה למנות ימי טומאה וימי טהרה אחרים לא ישוה לו לילה ליום נמי לחייבו קרבן שני:
notes.en: And Beit Hillel deem her liable: as they explain the reason: If the night of the eighty-first is equal to the eighty-first day with regard to impurity, for according to everyone she must count other days of impurity and days of purity, shall the night not be equal to the day also to make her liable to a second offering?

messages.text: No, there is a difference between that night and the following day. If you said with regard to a woman who miscarries on the eighty-first day that she is obligated to bring an additional offering, this is logical, as she emerged into a period that is fit for her to bring her offering. Would you say the same with regard to a woman who miscarries on the night of the eighty-first day, where she did not emerge into a period that is fit for her to bring her offering, as offerings are not sacrificed at night?

But let the case of a woman who miscarries on the eighty-first day that occurs on Shabbat prove that this distinction is incorrect, as she did not emerge into a period that is fit for her to bring her offering because individual offerings are not sacrificed on Shabbat, and nevertheless she is obligated to bring an additional offering.

notes.he: שלא יצא בשעה שראויה להביא בה קרבן דאין קרבן יחיד דוחה שבת וחייב בקרבן:
notes.en: Let the one that occurs on Shabbat prove it: for she did not emerge at a time fit to bring an offering, since an individual’s offering does not override Shabbat, and [yet] she is liable to the offering.

messages.text: No, there is a difference between these cases. If you said this ruling with regard to a woman who miscarries on the eighty-first day that occurs on Shabbat, the reason is that although Shabbat is unfit for the sacrifice of an individual offering, it is fit for the sacrifice of a communal offering whose time is fixed, e.g., the daily offering.

Would you say the same with regard to a woman who miscarries on the night of the eighty-first day, as the night is completely unfit, since neither an individual offering nor a communal offering is sacrificed at night?

And as for the ritual impurity status of the blood, i.e., Beit Hillel’s opinion that the two time periods are equal with regard to the halakhot of ritual impurity, this does not prove what the halakha should be with regard to offerings, as with regard to a woman who miscarries before the completion of the term of eighty days, her blood is impure like the blood of a woman after childbirth, and nevertheless she is exempt from bringing the offering.

notes.he: שאתה אומר אם שוה לו לטומאה כו' אינן מוכיחין לקרבן שהרי המפלת תוך מלאת דמיה טמאין מפני הלידה ואינה חייבת קרבן שני:
notes.en: And the blood: of which you say, “If they are equal with regard to impurity,” etc., does not prove [anything] for the offering, for one who miscarries within the completion [of her days], her blood is impure because of the birth, and she is not obligated to bring a second offering.

notes.he: הדמים שאתם אומרים אם שוה לו לטומאה אינן מוכיחין שהמפלת בתוך מלאות דמיה טמאין דצריכה להשלים ימי טומאה של מפלת לאחר פ' ופטור מן הקרבן הואיל ותוך מלאות הפילה:
notes.en: The blood, of which you say, “If they are equal with regard to impurity,” does not prove it, for one who miscarries within the completion [of her days], her blood is impure, as she must complete the days of impurity of a miscarriage after the eightieth [day], and she is exempt from the offering, since she miscarried within the completion.

messages.text: Continues on 8a: the Gemara opens with a baraita in which Beit Hillel cite the verse “for a son or for a daughter” to include the night of the eighty-first day.
